1.67.m: He should give a handful of flowers; afterwards he should perform the worship of the enclosures.

1.67.s:
yadāśābhimukho bhūtvā pūjanaṃ tu samācaret /
saiva prācī tu vijñeyā tato 'nyā vidiśo daśa //
1.67.d:
यदाशाभिमुखो भूत्वा पूजनं तु समाचरेत् ।
सैव प्राची तु विज्ञेया ततो ऽन्या विदिशो दश ॥
1.67.m: Facing whatever direction he performs the worship, / that should be known as the east, and after that the other ten intermediate directions.

1.67.s:
keśareṣvagnikoṇādi hṛdayādīni pūjayet /
netramagre dikṣu cāstraṃ aṅgamantrairyathākramam //
1.67.d:
केशरेष्वग्निकोणादि हृदयादीनि पूजयेत् ।
नेत्रमग्रे दिक्षु चास्त्रं अङ्गमन्त्रैर्यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.67.m: On the filaments [of the lotus], beginning from the fire corner (south-east), he should worship the heart and other [limbs]; / the eye in front, and the weapon in the [cardinal] directions, respectively with the limb-mantras.

1.67.s:
śuklaśvetasitaśyāmakṛṣṇaraktārciṣaḥ kramāt /
varābhayakarā dhyeyāḥ svasvadikṣvaṃ gaśaktayaḥ //
1.67.d:
शुक्लश्वेतसितश्यामकृष्णरक्तार्चिषः क्रमात् ।
वराभयकरा ध्येयाः स्वस्वदिक्ष्वं गशक्तयः ॥
1.67.m: White, fair, bright, dark, black, and red in their rays in order, / showing the gestures of bestowing boons and fearlessness, the limb-powers should be meditated on in their respective directions.

1.67.s:
amukāvaraṇānte tu devatā iti saṃvadet /
sālaṅkārāstataḥ paścātsāṃgāḥ saparicārikāḥ //
1.67.d:
अमुकावरणान्ते तु देवता इति संवदेत् ।
सालङ्कारास्ततः पश्चात्सांगाः सपरिचारिकाः ॥
1.67.m: At the end of [the name of] such-and-such an enclosure, he should say, ‘the deities’; / then adorned with ornaments, along with their limbs, along with their attendants,

1.67.s:
savāhanāḥ sāyudhāśca tataḥ sarvo pacārakaiḥ /
saṃpūjitāstarpitāśca varadāḥ saṃtvidaṃ paṭhet //
1.67.d:
सवाहनाः सायुधाश्च ततः सर्वो पचारकैः ।
संपूजितास्तर्पिताश्च वरदाः संत्विदं पठेत् ॥
1.67.m: with mounts and with weapons; then, worshipped with all the articles of worship / and propitiated, he should recite this: ‘Be granters of boons!’

1.67.s:
mūlānte ca samuñcārya divatāyai nivedayet /
abhīṣṭasiddhiṃ me dehi śaraṇāgatavatsala //
1.67.d:
मूलान्ते च समुञ्चार्य दिवतायै निवेदयेत् ।
अभीष्टसिद्धिं मे देहि शरणागतवत्सल ॥
1.67.m: Having pronounced [the formula] at the end of the root-mantra, he should announce to the deity: / ‘Grant me the attainment of my desired object, O you who are affectionate to those who seek refuge!

1.67.s:
bhaktayā samarpaye tubhyamamukāvaraṇārcanam /
ityuñcārya kṣipetpuṣpāñjaliṃ devasya mastake //
1.67.d:
भक्तया समर्पये तुभ्यममुकावरणार्चनम् ।
इत्युञ्चार्य क्षिपेत्पुष्पाञ्जलिं देवस्य मस्तके ॥
1.67.m: With devotion I offer to you the worship of such-and-such an enclosure.’ / Having pronounced this, he should throw a handful of flowers onto the head of the god.

1.67.s:
tatastvabhyarcyanīyāḥ syuḥ kalpoktāścāvṛtīḥ kramāt /
sāyudhāṃstata indrādyānsvasvadikṣu prapūjayet //
1.67.d:
ततस्त्वभ्यर्च्यनीयाः स्युः कल्पोक्ताश्चावृतीः क्रमात् ।
सायुधांस्तत इन्द्राद्यान्स्वस्वदिक्षु प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.67.m: Then the enclosures prescribed in the ritual injunction should be worshipped in succession; / then he should worship Indra and the others, accompanied by their weapons, in their respective directions:

1.67.s:
idro vahniryamo rakṣo varuṇaḥ pavano vidhuḥ /
īśāno 'tha vidhiścaivamadhastātpanna gādhipaḥ //
1.67.d:
इद्रो वह्निर्यमो रक्षो वरुणः पवनो विधुः ।
ईशानो ऽथ विधिश्चैवमधस्तात्पन्न गाधिपः ॥
1.67.m: Indra, Agni, Yama, the Rākṣasa (Nirṛti), Varuṇa, Pavana, the Moon, / Īśāna, and then Vidhi (Brahmā), and below the Lord of Serpents (Ananta).

1.67.s:
airāvatastathā meṣo mahiṣaḥ pretastimirmṛgaḥ /
vājī vṛṣo haṃsakūrmauṃ vāhanāni vidurbudhāḥ //
1.67.d:
ऐरावतस्तथा मेषो महिषः प्रेतस्तिमिर्मृगः ।
वाजी वृषो हंसकूर्मौं वाहनानि विदुर्बुधाः ॥
1.67.m: Airāvata, the ram, the buffalo, the corpse, the makara, the deer, / the horse, the bull, the goose, and the tortoise: the wise know [these to be] their mounts.

1.67.s:
vajraṃ śaktiṃ daṇḍakhaḍgau pāśāṃ kuśagadā api /
triśūlaṃ padmacakre ca kramādindrādihetayaḥ //
1.67.d:
वज्रं शक्तिं दण्डखड्गौ पाशां कुशगदा अपि ।
त्रिशूलं पद्मचक्रे च क्रमादिन्द्रादिहेतयः ॥
1.67.m: The thunderbolt, lance, staff, sword, noose, goad, mace, / trident, lotus, and discus in succession are the weapons of Indra and the others.

1.67.s:
samāpyāvaraṇārcāṃ tu devatārārtikaṃ caret /
śaṅkhatoyaṃ parikṣipyodvāhurnṛtyan patetkṣitau //
1.67.d:
समाप्यावरणार्चां तु देवतारार्तिकं चरेत् ।
शङ्खतोयं परिक्षिप्योद्वाहुर्नृत्यन् पतेत्क्षितौ ॥
1.67.m: Having completed the worship of the enclosures, he should perform the waving of lights before the deity; / having poured around conch water, raising his arms and dancing, he should fall to the earth.

1.67.s:
daṇḍavañcāpyathotthāya prārthayitvā nije śvaram /
dakṣiṇe sthaṇḍilaṃ kṛtvā tatra saṃskāramācaret //
1.67.d:
दण्डवञ्चाप्यथोत्थाय प्रार्थयित्वा निजे श्वरम् ।
दक्षिणे स्थण्डिलं कृत्वा तत्र संस्कारमाचरेत् ॥
1.67.m: Falling like a rod, and then rising, having prayed to his own Lord, / having prepared an altar on the right, he should perform the consecration there:

1.67.s:
mūlenekṣaṇamastreṇa prokṣaṇaṃ tāḍanaṃ punaḥ /
kuśaistadvarmaṇābhyukṣya pūjya tatra nyasedvasum //
1.67.d:
मूलेनेक्षणमस्त्रेण प्रोक्षणं ताडनं पुनः ।
कुशैस्तद्वर्मणाभ्युक्ष्य पूज्य तत्र न्यसेद्वसुम् ॥
1.67.m: Inspection with the root-mantra, sprinkling and striking with the weapon-mantra; / having sprinkled it with kuśa grass with the armour-mantra, and worshipped, he should deposit the fire there.

1.67.s:
pradāpya tatra juhuyāddhyātvā caiveṣṭadevatām /
mahāvyāhṛtibhiryastu samastābhiścatuṣṭayam //
1.67.d:
प्रदाप्य तत्र जुहुयाद्ध्यात्वा चैवेष्टदेवताम् ।
महाव्याहृतिभिर्यस्तु समस्ताभिश्चतुष्टयम् ॥
1.67.m: Having offered and having meditated on the chosen deity right there, / one who [offers] four [oblations] with all the great utterances combined,

1.67.s:
juhuyātsarpiṣā bhaktaistilairvā pāyasena vā /
saghṛtaiḥ sādhakaśreṣṭhaḥ pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā //
1.67.d:
जुहुयात्सर्पिषा भक्तैस्तिलैर्वा पायसेन वा ।
सघृतैः साधकश्रेष्ठः पञ्चविंशतिसंख्यया ॥
1.67.m: should make offerings with clarified butter, or cooked food, or sesame seeds, or milk-rice / with ghee, twenty-five in number, the best of practitioners.

1.67.s:
punarvyāhṛtibhaghirhutvā gandhādyaiḥ punararcayet /
devaṃ saṃyojayenmūrtauṃ tato vahniṃ visarjayet //
1.67.d:
पुनर्व्याहृतिभघिर्हुत्वा गन्धाद्यैः पुनरर्चयेत् ।
देवं संयोजयेन्मूर्तौं ततो वह्निं विसर्जयेत् ॥
1.67.m: Having offered again with the great utterances, he should worship again with perfumes and the rest; / he should unite the god in the image, and then dismiss the fire:

1.67.s:
bho bho vahne mahāśakte sarvakarmaprasādhaka /
karmāntare 'pi saṃprāpte sānnidhyaṃ kuru sādaram //
1.67.d:
भो भो वह्ने महाशक्ते सर्वकर्मप्रसाधक ।
कर्मान्तरे ऽपि संप्राप्ते सान्निध्यं कुरु सादरम् ॥
1.67.m: ‘O Fire! O you of great power, accomplisher of all rites! / Even when another rite has arrived, re-establish your presence with respect.’

1.67.s:
visṛjyāgnidevatāyai dadyādācamanīyakam /
avaśiṣṭena haviṣā gandhapuṣpākṣatānvitam //
1.67.d:
विसृज्याग्निदेवतायै दद्यादाचमनीयकम् ।
अवशिष्टेन हविषा गन्धपुष्पाक्षतान्वितम् ॥
1.67.m: Having dismissed [the fire], he should give water for sipping to the fire-deity, / along with the remaining oblation food accompanied by perfume, flowers, and unbroken rice.

1.67.s:
devatāpārṣadebhyo 'pi pūrvoktebhyo baliṃ dadet /
ye raudrā raudrakarmāṇo raudrasthānanivāsinaḥ //
1.67.d:
देवतापार्षदेभ्यो ऽपि पूर्वोक्तेभ्यो बलिं ददेत् ।
ये रौद्रा रौद्रकर्माणो रौद्रस्थाननिवासिनः ॥
1.67.m: One should offer a bali oblation to the attendants of the deity, who were mentioned earlier, / and to those who are fierce, performing fierce deeds and dwelling in fierce places,

1.67.s:
yoginyo hyugrarūpāśca gaṇānāmadhipāśca ye /
vighnabhūtāstathā cānye digvidikṣu samāśritāḥga //
1.67.d:
योगिन्यो ह्युग्ररूपाश्च गणानामधिपाश्च ये ।
विघ्नभूतास्तथा चान्ये दिग्विदिक्षु समाश्रिताःग ॥
1.67.m: and indeed to the yoginīs of terrible form, to the lords of the gaṇas, / and likewise to the other obstacle-spirits settled in the cardinal and intermediate directions:

1.67.s:
sarve te prītamanasaḥ pratigṛhṇantvimaṃ balim /
ityaṣṭadikṣu datvā ca punarbhūtabaliṃ caret //
1.67.d:
सर्वे ते प्रीतमनसः प्रतिगृह्णन्त्विमं बलिम् ।
इत्यष्टदिक्षु दत्वा च पुनर्भूतबलिं चरेत् ॥
1.67.m: "May all of them, with pleased minds, accept this bali oblation." / Having thus offered it in the eight directions, one should again perform the bali for the spirits.

1.67.s:
pānīyamamṛtīkṛtya mudrayā dhenusaṃjñayā /
devatāyāḥ kare dadyātpunaścācamanīyakam //
1.67.d:
पानीयममृतीकृत्य मुद्रया धेनुसंज्ञया ।
देवतायाः करे दद्यात्पुनश्चाचमनीयकम् ॥
1.67.m: Having transformed the water into nectar with the gesture called dhenu, / one should place it in the hand of the deity, and once again offer sipping-water.

1.67.s:
devamudvāsya mūrtisthaṃ punastatraiva yojayet /
naivedyaṃ ca tato dadyāttattaducchiṣṭabhojine //
1.67.d:
देवमुद्वास्य मूर्तिस्थं पुनस्तत्रैव योजयेत् ।
नैवेद्यं च ततो दद्यात्तत्तदुच्छिष्टभोजिने ॥
1.67.m: Having dismissed the god residing in the image, one should again unite him there; / and then one should offer food offerings to the respective consumer of the deity's leavings:

1.67.s:
maheśvarasya caṇḍeśo viṣvaksenastathā hareḥ /
caṇḍāṃśustaraṇervaktatuṇḍaścāpi gaṇeśituḥ /
śakterucchiṣṭacāṇḍālī proktā ucchiṣṭabhojinaḥ //
1.67.d:
महेश्वरस्य चण्डेशो विष्वक्सेनस्तथा हरेः ।
चण्डांशुस्तरणेर्वक्ततुण्डश्चापि गणेशितुः ।
शक्तेरुच्छिष्टचाण्डाली प्रोक्ता उच्छिष्टभोजिनः ॥
1.67.m: Caṇḍeśa is the consumer of the leavings for Maheśvara, and Viṣvaksena likewise for Hari; / Caṇḍāṃśu for the Sun, and Vakratuṇḍa for the lord of gaṇas; / Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālī is proclaimed for the Goddess.

1.67.s:
tato ṛṣyādikaṃ smṛtvā kṛtvā mūlaṣaḍaṅgakam /
japtvā mantraṃ yathāśakti devatāyai nivedayet //
1.67.d:
ततो ऋष्यादिकं स्मृत्वा कृत्वा मूलषडङ्गकम् ।
जप्त्वा मन्त्रं यथाशक्ति देवतायै निवेदयेत् ॥
1.67.m: Then, remembering the seer and other particulars, and performing the six limbs with the root [mantra], / having recited the mantra according to one's ability, one should dedicate it to the deity:

1.67.s:
guhyātiguhyagoptā tvaṃ gṛhāṇāsmatkṛtaṃ japam /
siddhirbhavatu me deva tvatprasādāttvayi sthitā //
1.67.d:
गुह्यातिगुह्यगोप्ता त्वं गृहाणास्मत्कृतं जपम् ।
सिद्धिर्भवतु मे देव त्वत्प्रसादात्त्वयि स्थिता ॥
1.67.m: "You are the protector of the most secret of secrets; accept the recitation performed by us. / May there be success for me, O God, abiding in You by Your grace."

1.67.s:
tataḥ parāṅmukhaṃ cārghaṃ kṛtvā puṣpaiḥ prapūjayet /
dorbhyāṃ pabhdyāṃ ca jānubhyāmurasā śirasādṛśā /
manasā vacasā ceti praṇāmo 'ṣṭāṅga īritaḥ //
1.67.d:
ततः पराङ्मुखं चार्घं कृत्वा पुष्पैः प्रपूजयेत् ।
दोर्भ्यां पभ्द्यां च जानुभ्यामुरसा शिरसादृशा ।
मनसा वचसा चेति प्रणामो ऽष्टाङ्ग ईरितः ॥
1.67.m: Then, having turned the arghya offering away, one should worship with flowers. / With the two arms, two feet, two knees, chest, head, and eyes, / with mind and speech—this is declared to be the eight-limbed prostration.

1.67.s:
bāhubhyāṃ ca sajānubhyāṃ śirasā vacasāpi vā /
pañcāṅgakaḥ praṇāmaḥ syātpūjāyāṃ pravarāvubhau //
1.67.d:
बाहुभ्यां च सजानुभ्यां शिरसा वचसापि वा ।
पञ्चाङ्गकः प्रणामः स्यात्पूजायां प्रवरावुभौ ॥
1.67.m: With the arms together with knees, with the head, or with speech: / that would be the five-limbed prostration; both are excellent in worship.

1.67.s:
natvā ca daṇḍavanmantrī tataḥ kuryātpradakṣiṇāḥ /
viṣmusomārkavighnānāṃ vedārdhendvadrivahnayaḥ //
1.67.d:
नत्वा च दण्डवन्मन्त्री ततः कुर्यात्प्रदक्षिणाः ।
विष्मुसोमार्कविघ्नानां वेदार्धेन्द्वद्रिवह्नयः ॥
1.67.m: Having bowed like a staff, the mantra practitioner should then circumambulate: / four times for Viṣṇu, one for the Moon, seven for the Sun, and three for Vighna.

1.67.s:
tataḥ stotrādikaṃ mantrī prapaṭhe dbhaktipūrvakam /
itaḥ pūrṇaṃ prāṇabuddhidehadharmādhikārataḥ //
1.67.d:
ततः स्तोत्रादिकं मन्त्री प्रपठे द्भक्तिपूर्वकम् ।
इतः पूर्णं प्राणबुद्धिदेहधर्माधिकारतः ॥
1.67.m: Then the mantra practitioner should recite a hymn of praise and similar texts with devotion: / "Henceforth fully, according to the authority of the duties of life-breath, intellect, and body,

1.67.s:
jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyante 'vasthāsu manasā vadet /
vācā hastābhyāṃ ca padbhyā mudareṇa tataḥ param //
1.67.d:
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्त्यन्ते ऽवस्थासु मनसा वदेत् ।
वाचा हस्ताभ्यां च पद्भ्या मुदरेण ततः परम् ॥
1.67.m: in the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, by the mind, / by speech, with the two hands, two feet, the belly, and thereafter

1.67.s:
śiṣṇānte yatsmṛtaṃ paścādyaduktaṃ yatkṛtaṃ tataḥ /
tatsarvaṃ ca tato brahmarpaṇaṃ bhavatu ṭhadvayam //
1.67.d:
शिष्णान्ते यत्स्मृतं पश्चाद्यदुक्तं यत्कृतं ततः ।
तत्सर्वं च ततो ब्रह्मर्पणं भवतु ठद्वयम् ॥
1.67.m: with the genitals—whatever was remembered, and then whatever was spoken, whatever was done— / may all that be an offering to Brahman, svāhā!"

1.67.s:
māṃ madīyaṃ ca sakalaṃ viṣṇave ca samarpaye /
tāraṃ tatsadato brahmarpaṇamastu manurmataḥ //
1.67.d:
मां मदीयं च सकलं विष्णवे च समर्पये ।
तारं तत्सदतो ब्रह्मर्पणमस्तु मनुर्मतः ॥
1.67.m: "I dedicate myself and all that is mine unto Viṣṇu. / Om tat sat, may this be an offering unto Brahman!"—this is considered the mantra.

1.67.s:
praṇavādyo 'ṣṭavasvarṇo hyanenātmānamarpayet /
ajñānādvā pramādādvā vaikalyātsādhanasya ca //
1.67.d:
प्रणवाद्यो ऽष्टवस्वर्णो ह्यनेनात्मानमर्पयेत् ।
अज्ञानाद्वा प्रमादाद्वा वैकल्यात्साधनस्य च ॥
1.67.m: Beginning with praṇava and having twenty-eight syllables: with this one should surrender oneself. / "Whether through ignorance, heedlessness, or deficiency of ritual means,

1.67.s:
yannyūnamatiriktaṃ vā tatsarvaṃ kṣantumarhasi /
dravyahīnaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ mantrahīnaṃ mayānyathā //
1.67.d:
यन्न्यूनमतिरिक्तं वा तत्सर्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि ।
द्रव्यहीनं क्रियाहीनं मन्त्रहीनं मयान्यथा ॥
1.67.m: whatever has been deficient or redundant, you ought to forgive all that. / Lacking ritual substances, lacking correct actions, lacking mantras, otherwise

1.67.s:
kṛtaṃ yattatkṣamasveśa kṛpayā tvaṃ dayānidhe /
yanmayā kriyate karma jāgratsvaprasuṣuptiṣu //
1.67.d:
कृतं यत्तत्क्षमस्वेश कृपया त्वं दयानिधे ।
यन्मया क्रियते कर्म जाग्रत्स्वप्रसुषुप्तिषु ॥
1.67.m: whatever was done by me: forgive that, O Lord, by your compassion, O ocean of mercy! / Whatever action is done by me in waking, dreaming, and deep sleep,

1.67.s:
tatsarvaṃ tāvakī pūjā bhūyādbhūtyai ca me prabho /
bhūmau skhalitapādānāṃ bhūmirevāvalaṃbanam //
1.67.d:
तत्सर्वं तावकी पूजा भूयाद्भूत्यै च मे प्रभो ।
भूमौ स्खलितपादानां भूमिरेवावलंबनम् ॥
1.67.m: may all that become your worship, and lead to my welfare, O Lord! / For those whose feet stumble on the ground, the ground itself is the support;

1.67.s:
tvayi jātāparādhānāṃ tvameva śaraṇaṃ prabho /
anyathā śaraṇaṃ nāsti tvameva śaraṇaṃ mama //
1.67.d:
त्वयि जातापराधानां त्वमेव शरणं प्रभो ।
अन्यथा शरणं नास्ति त्वमेव शरणं मम ॥
1.67.m: for those who have committed offenses against you, you alone are the refuge, O Lord! / There is no other refuge; you alone are my refuge.

1.67.s:
tasmātkāruṇyabhāvena kṣamasva parameśvara /
aparādhasahasrāṇi kriyante 'harnniśaṃ mayā //
1.67.d:
तस्मात्कारुण्यभावेन क्षमस्व परमेश्वर ।
अपराधसहस्राणि क्रियन्ते ऽहर्न्निशं मया ॥
1.67.m: Therefore, through the disposition of compassion, forgive me, O Supreme Lord! / Thousands of offenses are committed day and night by me;

1.67.s:
dāso 'yamiti māṃ matvā kṣamasva jagatāṃ pate /
āvāhanaṃ na jānāmi na jānāmi visarjanam //
1.67.d:
दासो ऽयमिति मां मत्वा क्षमस्व जगतां पते ।
आवाहनं न जानामि न जानामि विसर्जनम् ॥
1.67.m: thinking, 'This is my servant,' forgive me, O Lord of the worlds! / I do not know invocation, nor do I know dismissal;

1.67.s:
pūjāṃ caiva na jānāmi tvaṃ gatiḥ parameśvara /
saṃprārthyaivaṃ tato mantrī mūlānte ślokamuñcaret //
1.67.d:
पूजां चैव न जानामि त्वं गतिः परमेश्वर ।
संप्रार्थ्यैवं ततो मन्त्री मूलान्ते श्लोकमुञ्चरेत् ॥
1.67.m: and I do not know how to worship: you are my refuge, O Supreme Lord!" / Having thus prayed, the mantra practitioner should then recite the verse at the end of the root [mantra]:

1.67.s:
gaccha gaccha paraṃ sthānaṃ jagadīśa jaganmaya /
yanna brahmādayo devā jānanti ca sadāśivaḥ //
1.67.d:
गच्छ गच्छ परं स्थानं जगदीश जगन्मय ।
यन्न ब्रह्मादयो देवा जानन्ति च सदाशिवः ॥
1.67.m: "Go, go to the supreme abode, O Lord of the universe, who pervade the universe, / which the gods such as Brahmā do not know, nor Sadāśiva."

1.67.s:
iti puṣpāñjaliṃ datvā tataḥ saṃhāramudrayā /
nidhāya devaṃ sāṃgaṃ ca svīyadṛtsarasīruhe //
1.67.d:
इति पुष्पाञ्जलिं दत्वा ततः संहारमुद्रया ।
निधाय देवं सांगं च स्वीयदृत्सरसीरुहे ॥
1.67.m: Having thus offered a handful of flowers, then by means of the saṃhāramudrā, / placing the god together with his limbs in the lotus of one's own heart,

1.67.s:
suṣumṇāvartmanā puṣpamāghrāyodvāsayed budhaḥ /
śaṅkhacakraśilāliṅgavighnasūryadvayaṃ tathā //
1.67.d:
सुषुम्णावर्त्मना पुष्पमाघ्रायोद्वासयेद् बुधः ।
शङ्खचक्रशिलालिङ्गविघ्नसूर्यद्वयं तथा ॥
1.67.m: smelling the flower via the path of the suṣumṇā, the wise person should dismiss him. / Two conches, two cakras, two śālagrāma stones, two liṅgas, two Vighnas, two suns,

1.67.s:
śaktitrayaṃ na caikatra pūjayedduḥkhakāraṇam /
akālamṛtyuharaṇaṃ sarvavyādhivināśan //
1.67.d:
शक्तित्रयं न चैकत्र पूजयेद्दुःखकारणम् ।
अकालमृत्युहरणं सर्वव्याधिविनाशन् ॥
1.67.m: and three śaktis one should never worship together in one place; it causes sorrow. / Removing untimely death, destroying all diseases,

1.67.s: sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ viṣṇupādodakaṃ śubham //
1.67.d: सर्वपापक्षयकरं विष्णुपादोदकं शुभम् ॥
1.67.m: and effecting the destruction of all sins, is the auspicious water from Viṣṇu's feet.

1.67.s:
tattadbhaktairgṛhī tavyaṃ tannaivedyaniveditam /
agrāhyaṃ śivanirmālyaṃ patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ jalam //
1.67.d:
तत्तद्भक्तैर्गृही तव्यं तन्नैवेद्यनिवेदितम् ।
अग्राह्यं शिवनिर्माल्यं पत्रं पुष्पं फलं जलम् ॥
1.67.m: That which has been dedicated as a food offering should be received by the respective devotees. / Unacceptable are the offerings to Śiva: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water.

1.67.s:
śālagrāmaśilāsparśātsarvaṃ yāti pavitratām /
pūjā pañcavidhā tatra kathitā nāradākhilaiḥ //
1.67.d:
शालग्रामशिलास्पर्शात्सर्वं याति पवित्रताम् ।
पूजा पञ्चविधा तत्र कथिता नारदाखिलैः ॥
1.67.m: From contact with a śālagrāma stone, everything attains purity. / Worship has been declared there to be of five kinds by all, O Nārada:

1.67.s:
āturī sautikī trāsī sādhanā bhāvinī tathā /
daurbodhī ca kramādāsāṃ lakṣaṇāni śṛṇuṣaava me //
1.67.d:
आतुरी सौतिकी त्रासी साधना भाविनी तथा ।
दौर्बोधी च क्रमादासां लक्षणानि शृणुषअव मे ॥
1.67.m: āturī (the afflicted), sautikī (of impurity), trāsī (of fear), sādhanābhāvinī (of lacking means), / and daurbodhī (of ignorance). Hear from me their characteristics in due order.

1.67.s:
rogādiyukto na srāyānna japenna ca pūjayet /
vilokya pūjāṃ devasya mūrtiṃ vā sūryyamaṇḍalam //
1.67.d:
रोगादियुक्तो न स्रायान्न जपेन्न च पूजयेत् ।
विलोक्य पूजां देवस्य मूर्तिं वा सूर्य्यमण्डलम् ॥
1.67.m: One afflicted with illness or the like should not bathe, should not recite, and should not worship. / Having beheld the worship of the god, or the image, or the orb of the sun,

1.67.s:
praṇamyātha smaranmantramarpayetkumāñjalim /
roge nivṛtte snātvātha natvā saṃpūñcedgurum //
1.67.d:
प्रणम्याथ स्मरन्मन्त्रमर्पयेत्कुमाञ्जलिम् ।
रोगे निवृत्ते स्नात्वाथ नत्वा संपूञ्चेद्गुरुम् ॥
1.67.m: having bowed and then remembering the mantra, one should offer a handful of flowers. / When the illness has ceased, having bathed, bowed, and worshipped the guru,

1.67.s:
tvatprasādājjagannātha jagatpūjya dayānidhe /
pūjāvicchedadoṣo me māstviti prārthayecca tam //
1.67.d:
त्वत्प्रसादाज्जगन्नाथ जगत्पूज्य दयानिधे ।
पूजाविच्छेददोषो मे मास्त्विति प्रार्थयेच्च तम् ॥
1.67.m: one should pray to him: "By your grace, O Lord of the world, worthy of the world's worship, O ocean of mercy, / may there be no fault on my part for interrupting the worship."

1.67.s:
dvijānapi ca saṃpūjya yathāśaktyā pratoṣya ca /
tebhyaścāśiṣamādāya devaṃ prāgvattator'cayet //
1.67.d:
द्विजानपि च संपूज्य यथाशक्त्या प्रतोष्य च ।
तेभ्यश्चाशिषमादाय देवं प्राग्वत्ततोर्ऽचयेत् ॥
1.67.m: Having worshipped the twice-born also, pleasing them according to one's ability, / and receiving blessings from them, one should then worship the god as before.

1.67.s:
āturī kathitā hyeṣā sotikyatha nigadyate /
sūtakaṃ dvividhaṃ proktaṃ jātākhyaṃ mṛtasaṃjñakam //
1.67.d:
आतुरी कथिता ह्येषा सोतिक्यथ निगद्यते ।
सूतकं द्विविधं प्रोक्तं जाताख्यं मृतसंज्ञकम् ॥
1.67.m: This has indeed been declared as āturī; now sautikī is described. / Impurity is said to be of two kinds: that called birth-impurity and that called death-impurity.

1.67.s:
tatra snātvā mānasīṃ tu kṛtvā saṃdhyāṃ samāhitaḥ /
manasaiva yajeddevaṃ manasaiva japenmanum //
1.67.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा मानसीं तु कृत्वा संध्यां समाहितः ।
मनसैव यजेद्देवं मनसैव जपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.67.m: There, having bathed and performed the twilight worship mentally, concentrated in mind, / one should worship the god solely with the mind and recite the mantra solely with the mind.

1.67.s:
nivṛtte sūtake prāgvatsaṃpūjya ca guruṃ dvijān /
tebhyaścāśiṣamādāya tato nityakramaṃ caret //
1.67.d:
निवृत्ते सूतके प्राग्वत्संपूज्य च गुरुं द्विजान् ।
तेभ्यश्चाशिषमादाय ततो नित्यक्रमं चरेत् ॥
1.67.m: When the impurity has ended, having worshipped the guru and the twice-born as before, / and receiving blessings from them, one should then perform the daily sequence.

1.67.s:
eṣā tu sautikī proktā trāsī cātha nigadyate /
duṣṭebhyastrāsamāpanno yathālabdhopacāraṅkaiḥ //
1.67.d:
एषा तु सौतिकी प्रोक्ता त्रासी चाथ निगद्यते ।
दुष्टेभ्यस्त्रासमापन्नो यथालब्धोपचारङ्कैः ॥
1.67.m: This is proclaimed as sautikī; now trāsī is described. / One who has incurred terror from wicked persons, using whatever offerings are available,

1.67.s:
mānasairvai yajeddevaṃ trāsī sā parikīrtitā /
pūjāsādhanavastūnāma sāmarthye tu sarvataḥ //
1.67.d:
मानसैर्वै यजेद्देवं त्रासी सा परिकीर्तिता ।
पूजासाधनवस्तूनाम सामर्थ्ये तु सर्वतः ॥
1.67.m: or indeed through mental ones, should worship the god: that is celebrated as trāsī. / When there is total incapacity with regard to the articles for worship,

1.67.s:
puṣpaiḥ patraiḥ phalairvāpi manasā vā yajedvibhum /
sādhanābhāvinī hyeṣā daurbodhīṃ śṛṇu nārada //
1.67.d:
पुष्पैः पत्रैः फलैर्वापि मनसा वा यजेद्विभुम् ।
साधनाभाविनी ह्येषा दौर्बोधीं शृणु नारद ॥
1.67.m: one should worship the all-pervading Lord with flowers, leaves, fruits, or even with the mind: / this is sādhanābhāvinī. Hear of daurbodhī, O Nārada.

1.67.s:
striyo vṛddhā stathā bālā mūrkhāstaistu yathākramam /
yathājñānakṛtā sā tu daurbodhīti prakīrtitā //
1.67.d:
स्त्रियो वृद्धा स्तथा बाला मूर्खास्तैस्तु यथाक्रमम् ।
यथाज्ञानकृता सा तु दौर्बोधीति प्रकीर्तिता ॥
1.67.m: Worship performed by women, the elderly, children, and fools, according to their capacity, / in accordance with their limited knowledge, is celebrated as daurbodhī.

1.67.s:
evaṃ yathākathañcittu pūjāṃ kuryāddhi sādhakaḥ /
devapūjāvihīno yaḥ sa gacchennarakaṃ dhruvam //
1.67.d:
एवं यथाकथञ्चित्तु पूजां कुर्याद्धि साधकः ।
देवपूजाविहीनो यः स गच्छेन्नरकं ध्रुवम् ॥
1.67.m: Thus, somehow or other, the practitioner should indeed perform worship; / one who is destitute of worship of God surely goes to hell.

1.67.s:
vaiśvadevādikaṃ kṛtvā bhojayeddvijasattamān /
deve niveditaṃ paścādbhuñjīta svagaṇaiḥ svayam //
1.67.d:
वैश्वदेवादिकं कृत्वा भोजयेद्द्विजसत्तमान् ।
देवे निवेदितं पश्चाद्भुञ्जीत स्वगणैः स्वयम् ॥
1.67.m: Having performed the vaiśvadeva and other rites, one should feed the best of the twice-born; / afterwards, one should oneself eat together with one's dependents what was offered to the god.

1.67.s:
ācamyānanaśuddhiṃ ca kṛtvā tiṣṭet kiyatkṣaṇam /
purāṇamitihāsaṃ ca śṛṇuyātsvajanaiḥ saha //
1.67.d:
आचम्याननशुद्धिं च कृत्वा तिष्टेत् कियत्क्षणम् ।
पुराणमितिहासं च शृणुयात्स्वजनैः सह ॥
1.67.m: Having sipped water and cleansed the mouth, one should sit for a few moments, / and listen to a Purāṇa and Itihāsa together with one's kin.

1.67.s:
samarthaḥ sarvakalpeṣu yo 'nukalpaṃ samācaret /
na sāṃgaśayikaṃ tasya durmaterjāyate phalam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde devapūjānirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptaṣaṣṭittamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.67.d:
समर्थः सर्वकल्पेषु यो ऽनुकल्पं समाचरेत् ।
न सांगशयिकं तस्य दुर्मतेर्जायते फलम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे देवपूजानिरूपणं नाम सप्तषष्टित्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.67.m:
One who, being capable of all the primary rules, resorts to a secondary rule, / is of corrupted mind; no fruit of his, accompanied by all limbs, is produced.

Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter, named "Ascertainment of the Worship of the Deity", in the Third Quarter of the Great Narrative in the First Part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.68.s:
śrīsanatkumāra uvāca /
atha vakṣye gaṇeśasya mantrānsarveṣṭadāyakān /
yānsamārādhya viprendra sādhako bhuktimuktimān //
1.68.d:
श्रीसनत्कुमार उवाच ।
अथ वक्ष्ये गणेशस्य मन्त्रान्सर्वेष्टदायकान् ।
यान्समाराध्य विप्रेन्द्र साधको भुक्तिमुक्तिमान् ॥
1.68.m: Illustrious Sanatkumāra said: / Now I shall declare the mantras of Gaṇeśa that grant all desires, / by worshipping which, O best of vipras, the practitioner obtains enjoyment and liberation.

1.68.s:
avyayo viṣṇuvanitā śaṃbhustrī mīnaketanaḥ /
smṛtirmāṃseṃdumanvāḍhyā sā punaścandraśekharā //
1.68.d:
अव्ययो विष्णुवनिता शंभुस्त्री मीनकेतनः ।
स्मृतिर्मांसेंदुमन्वाढ्या सा पुनश्चन्द्रशेखरा ॥
1.68.m: The imperishable [oṃ], the consort of Viṣṇu [śrīm], the wife of Śambhu [hrīm], the fish-bannered [klīm], / memory endowed with meat and moon [glaum], and that adorned with the crest-moon [gam],

1.68.s:
ṅeṃto gaṇapatistoyaṃ bhujaṅgo varadeti ca /
sarvānte janamuñcārya tato me vaśamānaya //
1.68.d:
ङेंतो गणपतिस्तोयं भुजङ्गो वरदेति च ।
सर्वान्ते जनमुञ्चार्य ततो मे वशमानय ॥
1.68.m: Gaṇapati ending in ṅe [gaṇapataye], water [vara], snake [varada], and 'grant boons' [varada], / after all uttering 'people' [sarvajanam], and then 'bring into my control' [me vaśam ānaya],

1.68.s:
vahniḥ priyānto mantro 'yaṣṭāviṃśativarṇavān /
gaṇako 'sya muniśchando gāyatrī viyudādikā //
1.68.d:
वह्निः प्रियान्तो मन्त्रो ऽयष्टाविंशतिवर्णवान् ।
गणको ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो गायत्री वियुदादिका ॥
1.68.m: ending with the beloved of fire [svāhā]—this mantra consists of twenty-eight syllables. / Its sage is Gaṇaka; the meter is Gāyatrī beginning with viyad;

1.68.s:
gaṇeśo devatā bījaṃ ṣaṣṭaśaktistadādikā /
śrīmanmahāgaṇapatiprītaye viniyogakaḥ //
1.68.d:
गणेशो देवता बीजं षष्टशक्तिस्तदादिका ।
श्रीमन्महागणपतिप्रीतये विनियोगकः ॥
1.68.m: Gaṇeśa is the deity; the seed is the sixth [gam]; the power is that which begins it [śrīm]; / the application is for the pleasing of the glorious Mahāgaṇapati.

1.68.s:
ṛṣiṃ śirasi vakre tu chandaśca hṛdi devatām /
guhye bījaṃ padoḥ śaktiṃ nyasetsādhakasattamaḥ //
1.68.d:
ऋषिं शिरसि वक्रे तु छन्दश्च हृदि देवताम् ।
गुह्ये बीजं पदोः शक्तिं न्यसेत्साधकसत्तमः ॥
1.68.m: The sage on the head, the meter on the mouth, the deity on the heart, / the seed on the private parts, and the power on the feet: the best of practitioners should place them.

1.68.s:
ṣaḍdīrghāḍhyena bījena yaṃ ca bījādinā punaḥ /
ṣaḍaṅgāni nyasedasya jātiyuktāni mantravit //
1.68.d:
षड्दीर्घाढ्येन बीजेन यं च बीजादिना पुनः ।
षडङ्गानि न्यसेदस्य जातियुक्तानि मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.68.m: With the seed endowed with the six long vowels, and again with the seed and the rest, / the knower of mantra should place its six limbs endowed with their endings.

1.68.s:
śaivī ṣaḍaṅgamudrāya nyastavyā hi ṣaḍaṅgake /
gāmādyaṃ caiva bhūrlokaṃ nābhyantaṃ pādayornyaset //
1.68.d:
शैवी षडङ्गमुद्राय न्यस्तव्या हि षडङ्गके ।
गामाद्यं चैव भूर्लोकं नाभ्यन्तं पादयोर्न्यसेत् ॥
1.68.m: The Śaivite six-limb gesture must be applied to the six limbs. / One should place Bhūrloka beginning with 'gām' from the feet up to the navel;

1.68.s:
gīmādyaṃ ca bhuvarlokaṃ kaṇṭhāntaṃ nābhito nyaset /
svarlokaṃ caiva gūmādyaṃ kaṇṭhadimastakāvadhi //
1.68.d:
गीमाद्यं च भुवर्लोकं कण्ठान्तं नाभितो न्यसेत् ।
स्वर्लोकं चैव गूमाद्यं कण्ठदिमस्तकावधि ॥
1.68.m: and Bhuvarloka beginning with 'gīm' from the navel up to the throat; / and Svarloka beginning with 'gūm' from the throat up to the head.

1.68.s:
vyāpakaṃ mūlamantreṇa nyāso 'yaṃ bhuvanābhidhaḥ /
mūlamantraṃ samuñcārya mātṛkāvarṇamīrayet //
1.68.d:
व्यापकं मूलमन्त्रेण न्यासो ऽयं भुवनाभिधः ।
मूलमन्त्रं समुञ्चार्य मातृकावर्णमीरयेत् ॥
1.68.m: Then an all-pervading [placement] with the root mantra; this is the placement named bhuvanā. / Uttering the root mantra, one should recite the mātṛkā letter;

1.68.s:
tadante 'pi ca mūlaṃ syānnamoṃ'taṃ mātṛkāsthale /
kṣāntaṃ vinyasya mūlena vyāpakaṃ racayetsudhīḥ //
1.68.d:
तदन्ते ऽपि च मूलं स्यान्नमोंऽतं मातृकास्थले ।
क्षान्तं विन्यस्य मूलेन व्यापकं रचयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.68.m: at its end too should be the root mantra, ending with 'namaḥ', at the site of the mātṛkā. / Placing [them] up to 'kṣa', the wise one should perform an all-pervading [placement] with the root mantra.

1.68.s:
varṇanyā so 'yamākhyātaḥ padanyāsastathocyate /
pañcatribāṇavahnīnducandrākṣinigamaiḥ kramāt //
1.68.d:
वर्णन्या सो ऽयमाख्यातः पदन्यासस्तथोच्यते ।
पञ्चत्रिबाणवह्नीन्दुचन्द्राक्षिनिगमैः क्रमात् ॥
1.68.m: This is described as the placement of syllables; now the placement of words is declared: / By five, three, five, three, one, one, two, and four in order,

1.68.s:
vibhaktairmūlagāyatryā hṛdantairaṣṭabhiḥ padaiḥ /
bhāladeśe mukhe kaṇṭhe hṛdi nābhyūrujānuṣu //
1.68.d:
विभक्तैर्मूलगायत्र्या हृदन्तैरष्टभिः पदैः ।
भालदेशे मुखे कण्ठे हृदि नाभ्यूरुजानुषु ॥
1.68.m: divided by the eight words of the root gāyatrī ending with 'hṛd', / on the forehead, the mouth, the throat, the heart, the navel, thighs, and knees,

1.68.s:
pādayoścaiva vinyasya mūlane vyāpakaṃ caret /
vadettatpuruṣāyānte vidmaheti padaṃ tataḥ //
1.68.d:
पादयोश्चैव विन्यस्य मूलने व्यापकं चरेत् ।
वदेत्तत्पुरुषायान्ते विद्महेति पदं ततः ॥
1.68.m: and placing on the two feet, one should perform an all-pervading [placement] with the root mantra. / One should say the word 'tatpuruṣāya', and next 'vidmahe';

1.68.s:
vakratuṇḍāya śabdānte dhīmahīti samīrayet /
tanno dantiḥ pracovarṇā dayāditi vadetpunaḥ //
1.68.d:
वक्रतुण्डाय शब्दान्ते धीमहीति समीरयेत् ।
तन्नो दन्तिः प्रचोवर्णा दयादिति वदेत्पुनः ॥
1.68.m: after the words 'vakratuṇḍāya', one should utter 'dhīmahi'; / 'tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt' one should say next.

1.68.s:
eṣoktā mūlagāyatrī sarvasiddhipradāyinī /
evaṃ nyāsavidhiṃ kṛtvā dhyāyedevaṃ hṛdaṃbuje //
1.68.d:
एषोक्ता मूलगायत्री सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायिनी ।
एवं न्यासविधिं कृत्वा ध्यायेदेवं हृदंबुजे ॥
1.68.m: This is declared to be the root gāyatrī, the giver of all attainments. / Having performed this procedure of ritual placement, one should meditate in this manner in the lotus of the heart:

1.68.s:
udyanmārtaṇḍasadṛśaṃ lokasthityantakāraṇam /
saśaktikaṃ bhūṣitāṅgaṃ danta cakrādyudāyudham //
1.68.d:
उद्यन्मार्तण्डसदृशं लोकस्थित्यन्तकारणम् ।
सशक्तिकं भूषिताङ्गं दन्त चक्राद्युदायुधम् ॥
1.68.m: Resembling the rising sun, the cause of the preservation and destruction of the world, / accompanied by his śakti, his limbs adorned, raising weapons beginning with the tusk and discus.

1.68.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā catuścatvāriṃśatsāhasrasaṃyutam /
caturlakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ aṣṭadravyairdaśāṃśataḥ //
1.68.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा चतुश्चत्वारिंशत्साहस्रसंयुतम् ।
चतुर्लक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं अष्टद्रव्यैर्दशांशतः ॥
1.68.m: Having meditated thus, one should recite the mantra four hundred and forty-four thousand times. / With eight substances, one-tenth [of the total]

1.68.s:
juhuyādvidhivanmantrī saṃskṛte havyavāhane /
ikṣavaḥ saktavo mocāphalāni cipiṭāstilāḥ //
1.68.d:
जुहुयाद्विधिवन्मन्त्री संस्कृते हव्यवाहने ।
इक्षवः सक्तवो मोचाफलानि चिपिटास्तिलाः ॥
1.68.m: the mantra-practitioner should offer in fire oblation according to rule into consecrated fire. / Sugarcanes, barley flour, plantains, flattened rice, sesame seeds,

1.68.s:
modakā nārikelāni lājā dravyāṣṭakaṃ smṛtam /
pīṭhamādhāraśaktyādiparatatvāntamarcayet //
1.68.d:
मोदका नारिकेलानि लाजा द्रव्याष्टकं स्मृतम् ।
पीठमाधारशक्त्यादिपरतत्वान्तमर्चयेत् ॥
1.68.m: modakas, coconuts, and puffed grain: this is remembered as the group of eight substances. / One should worship the ritual seat from the base-power up to the supreme reality.

1.68.s:
ṣaṭkoṇāntastrikoṇaṃ ca bahiraṣṭadalaṃ likhet /
bhūpuraṃ tadbahiḥ kṛtvā gameśaṃ tatra pūjayet //
1.68.d:
षट्कोणान्तस्त्रिकोणं च बहिरष्टदलं लिखेत् ।
भूपुरं तद्बहिः कृत्वा गमेशं तत्र पूजयेत् ॥
1.68.m: One should draw a triangle within a six-pointed star, and outside an eight-petalled [lotus]; / having made an earth-enclosure outside that, one should worship Gaṇeśa there.

1.68.s:
tīvrākhyā jvālinī nandā bhogadā kāmarūpāṇī /
agrā tejovatī satyā navamī vidhnanāśinī //
1.68.d:
तीव्राख्या ज्वालिनी नन्दा भोगदा कामरूपाणी ।
अग्रा तेजोवती सत्या नवमी विध्ननाशिनी ॥
1.68.m: Tīvrā, Jvālinī, Nandā, Bhogadā, Kāmarūpiṇī, / Ugrā, Tejovatī, Satyā, and ninth, Vighnanāśinī.

1.68.s:
sarvādiśaktikamalāsanāya hṛdayāntikaḥ /
pīṭhamantro 'yametena dadyādāsanamuttamam //
1.68.d:
सर्वादिशक्तिकमलासनाय हृदयान्तिकः ।
पीठमन्त्रो ऽयमेतेन दद्यादासनमुत्तमम् ॥
1.68.m: 'To the lotus-seat of all primordial powers' ending with hṛdaya ['namaḥ']— / this is the seat-mantra; with this, one should offer the excellent seat.

1.68.s:
tatrāvāhya gaṇādhīśaṃ madhye sampūjya yatnataḥ /
vikoṇabāhye pūrvādicaturdikṣaavarcayetkramāt //
1.68.d:
तत्रावाह्य गणाधीशं मध्ये सम्पूज्य यत्नतः ।
विकोणबाह्ये पूर्वादिचतुर्दिक्षअवर्चयेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.68.m: Invoking the Lord of the Ganas there, and carefully worshipping him in the center, / outside the triangle, in the four directions beginning with the east, one should worship in order:

1.68.s:
śriyaṃ śriyaḥ patiṃ caiva gaurīṃ gaurī patiṃ tathā /
ratiṃ ratipatiṃ pāścānmahīpūrva ca potriṇam //
1.68.d:
श्रियं श्रियः पतिं चैव गौरीं गौरी पतिं तथा ।
रतिं रतिपतिं पाश्चान्महीपूर्व च पोत्रिणम् ॥
1.68.m: Śrī and the husband of Śrī; Gaurī and the husband of Gaurī; / Rati and the husband of Rati; and next, the Earth and the Boar.

1.68.s:
kramādilvavaṭāśvatthapriyagūnāmadhor'cayet /
ramā padmadvayakarā śaṅkhacakradharo hariḥ //
1.68.d:
क्रमादिल्ववटाश्वत्थप्रियगूनामधोर्ऽचयेत् ।
रमा पद्मद्वयकरा शङ्खचक्रधरो हरिः ॥
1.68.m: In order, one should worship them beneath bilva, banyan, peepal, and priyaṅgu trees. / Ramā has two lotuses in her hands; Hari holds a conch and a discus.

1.68.s:
gaurī pāśāṅkuśadharā ṭaṅkaśūladharo haraḥ /
ratiḥ padmakarā puṣpabāṇacāpadharaḥ smaraḥ //
1.68.d:
गौरी पाशाङ्कुशधरा टङ्कशूलधरो हरः ।
रतिः पद्मकरा पुष्पबाणचापधरः स्मरः ॥
1.68.m: Gaurī holds a noose and a goad; Hara holds a chisel and a trident. / Rati has a lotus in her hand; Smara holds a flower-arrow and a bow.

1.68.s:
śūkavrīhyagrahastā bhūḥ potrī cakragadādharaḥ /
devāgre pūjayellakṣmīsahitaṃ tu vināyakam //
1.68.d:
शूकव्रीह्यग्रहस्ता भूः पोत्री चक्रगदाधरः ।
देवाग्रे पूजयेल्लक्ष्मीसहितं तु विनायकम् ॥
1.68.m: The Earth holds awns and the tops of grain in her hands; the Boar holds a discus and a mace. / Before the deity, one should worship Vināyaka accompanied by Lakṣmī.

1.68.s:
pūjayetṣaṭsu koṇeṣu hyāmodādyānpriyāyutān /
āmodaṃ siddhisaṃyuktamagrataḥ paripījayet //
1.68.d:
पूजयेत्षट्सु कोणेषु ह्यामोदाद्यान्प्रियायुतान् ।
आमोदं सिद्धिसंयुक्तमग्रतः परिपीजयेत् ॥
1.68.m: In the six corners, one should worship those beginning with Āmoda together with their beloveds. / One should worship Āmoda endowed with Siddhi in front;

1.68.s:
pramodaṃ cāgnikoṇe tu samṛddhisahitaṃ yajet /
īśakoṇe yajetkīrtisaṃyutaṃ sumukhaṃ tathā //
1.68.d:
प्रमोदं चाग्निकोणे तु समृद्धिसहितं यजेत् ।
ईशकोणे यजेत्कीर्तिसंयुतं सुमुखं तथा ॥
1.68.m: and Pramoda endowed with Samṛddhi in the fire corner [southeast]; / in the northeast corner, one should worship Sumukha accompanied by Kīrti;

1.68.s:
vāruṇe madanāvatyā saṃyutaṃ durmukhaṃ yajet /
yajennairṛtyakoṇe tu vighnaṃ madadravāyutam //
1.68.d:
वारुणे मदनावत्या संयुतं दुर्मुखं यजेत् ।
यजेन्नैरृत्यकोणे तु विघ्नं मदद्रवायुतम् ॥
1.68.m: in the western direction, one should worship Durmukha endowed with Madanāvatī; / in the southwest corner, one should worship Vighna accompanied by Madadravā;

1.68.s:
drāviṇyā vighnakartāraṃ vāyukoṇe samarcayet /
pāśāṅkuśābhayakarāṃstaruṇārkasamaprabhān //
1.68.d:
द्राविण्या विघ्नकर्तारं वायुकोणे समर्चयेत् ।
पाशाङ्कुशाभयकरांस्तरुणार्कसमप्रभान् ॥
1.68.m: in the wind corner [northwest], one should worship Vighnakartṛ with Drāviṇī. / Holding a noose, a goad, and granting fearlessness with their hands, radiant as the morning sun,

1.68.s:
kapolavigaladdānagandhalubdhā liśobhitān /
ṣaṭkoṇobhayapārśve tu śaṅkhapadmanibhau kramāt //
1.68.d:
कपोलविगलद्दानगन्धलुब्धा लिशोभितान् ।
षट्कोणोभयपार्श्वे तु शङ्खपद्मनिभौ क्रमात् ॥
1.68.m: adorned with bees attracted by the scent of ichor trickling from their temples; / and on both sides of the six-pointed star, those resembling Conch and Lotus in order,

1.68.s:
sahitau nijaśaktibhyāṃ dhyātvā pūrvavadarcayet /
keśareṣu ṣaḍaṅgāni patreṣvaṣṭau tu mātaraḥ //
1.68.d:
सहितौ निजशक्तिभ्यां ध्यात्वा पूर्ववदर्चयेत् ।
केशरेषु षडङ्गानि पत्रेष्वष्टौ तु मातरः ॥
1.68.m: accompanied by their own śaktis, having meditated [on them], one should worship as before. / The six limbs on the filaments, and the eight Mothers on the petals,

1.68.s:
indrādyānapi vajjrādīnpūjayeddharaṇīgṛhe /
evamārādhya vighneśaṃ sādhayetsvamanorathān //
1.68.d:
इन्द्राद्यानपि वज्ज्रादीन्पूजयेद्धरणीगृहे ।
एवमाराध्य विघ्नेशं साधयेत्स्वमनोरथान् ॥
1.68.m: and Indra and the others, as well as the thunderbolt and other [weapons], one should worship in the earth-enclosure. / Having worshipped the Lord of Obstacles in this way, one achieves one's desires.

1.68.s:
catuścatvāriṃśatāḍhyaṃ catuḥ śatamatandritaḥ /
tarpayedaṃbubhiḥ śuddhairgajāsyaṃ dinaśaḥ sudhīḥ //
1.68.d:
चतुश्चत्वारिंशताढ्यं चतुः शतमतन्द्रितः ।
तर्पयेदंबुभिः शुद्धैर्गजास्यं दिनशः सुधीः ॥
1.68.m: Four hundred and forty-four times, unwearied, / the wise one should daily offer water-libation to the elephant-faced god with pure waters.

1.68.s:
padmaistu vaśayedbhūpāṃstatpatnīścotpalaistathā /
kumudairmantriṇo 'śvatthasamidbhirvāḍavāñśubhaiḥ //
1.68.d:
पद्मैस्तु वशयेद्भूपांस्तत्पत्नीश्चोत्पलैस्तथा ।
कुमुदैर्मन्त्रिणो ऽश्वत्थसमिद्भिर्वाडवाञ्शुभैः ॥
1.68.m: With lotuses he should subjugate kings, and with blue water-lilies their queens; / with white water-lilies ministers, and with auspicious peepal fuel-sticks brāhmaṇas;

1.68.s:
uduṃmbarotthairnṛpatīnvaiśyānplakṣasamudbhavaiḥ /
vaṭodbhavaiḥ samidbhiśca vaśayedantimānbudhaḥ //
1.68.d:
उदुंम्बरोत्थैर्नृपतीन्वैश्यान्प्लक्षसमुद्भवैः ।
वटोद्भवैः समिद्भिश्च वशयेदन्तिमान्बुधः ॥
1.68.m: with those from the udumbara, kings; with those from the plakṣa, vaiśyas; / and with fuel-sticks from the banyan tree, the wise one should subjugate the last [varṇa].

1.68.s:
ājyena śriyamāpnoti svarṇāptirmadhunā bhavet /
godugdhena gavāṃ lābho dadhnā sarvasamṛddhimān //
1.68.d:
आज्येन श्रियमाप्नोति स्वर्णाप्तिर्मधुना भवेत् ।
गोदुग्धेन गवां लाभो दध्ना सर्वसमृद्धिमान् ॥
1.68.m: Through ghee one attains fortune; the acquisition of gold comes through honey; / through cow's milk the obtaining of cattle; through curd one obtains all prosperity.

1.68.s:
annāptirannahomena samidbhirvetasāṃ jalam /
vāsāṃsi labhate hutvā kusuṃbhakusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.68.d:
अन्नाप्तिरन्नहोमेन समिद्भिर्वेतसां जलम् ।
वासांसि लभते हुत्वा कुसुंभकुसुमैः शुभैः ॥
1.68.m: The obtaining of food comes through food-oblations; with fuel-sticks of the reed, water; / by offering oblations with auspicious safflower flowers, one obtains garments.

1.68.s:
atha sarveṣṭadaṃ vakṣye caturāvṛttitarpaṇam /
mūlenādau caturvāraṃ pratyekaṃ ca pratarpayet //
1.68.d:
अथ सर्वेष्टदं वक्ष्ये चतुरावृत्तितर्पणम् ।
मूलेनादौ चतुर्वारं प्रत्येकं च प्रतर्पयेत् ॥
1.68.m: Now I shall declare the fourfold libation that bestows all desires: / At first, with the root mantra, one should offer libation four times for each,

1.68.s:
pūrvamantrākṣarairmantraiḥ svāhāntaiśca catuścatuḥ /
mūlamantraiścaturvārapūrvakaṃ saṃpratarpya ca //
1.68.d:
पूर्वमन्त्राक्षरैर्मन्त्रैः स्वाहान्तैश्च चतुश्चतुः ।
मूलमन्त्रैश्चतुर्वारपूर्वकं संप्रतर्प्य च ॥
1.68.m: with mantras of the syllables of the former mantra ending with 'svāhā', four by four; / having offered libations preceded by four times with the root mantras,

1.68.s:
mithunādīṃstataḥ paścātpūrvavatsaṃpratarpayet /
devena sahitāṃ śaktiṃ śaktyā ca sahitaṃ tu tam //
1.68.d:
मिथुनादींस्ततः पश्चात्पूर्ववत्संप्रतर्पयेत् ।
देवेन सहितां शक्तिं शक्त्या च सहितं तु तम् ॥
1.68.m: one should then offer libations as before to the couples and others: / to the śakti accompanied by the god, and to him accompanied by the śakti.

1.68.s:
evañca ṣaḍviṃśatidhā mithunāni bhavanti hi /
svanāmādyarṇabījāni tāni santarpayetkramāt //
1.68.d:
एवञ्च षड्विंशतिधा मिथुनानि भवन्ति हि ।
स्वनामाद्यर्णबीजानि तानि सन्तर्पयेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.68.m: In this manner, there are twenty-six couples; / one should offer libations to them in order, using the seed-syllables that begin their own names.

1.68.s:
bhavetsaṃbhūya sacatuścatvāriṃśañcatuḥ śatam /
evaṃ saṃtapya tatpaścātpūrvavatsopacārakaiḥ //
1.68.d:
भवेत्संभूय सचतुश्चत्वारिंशञ्चतुः शतम् ।
एवं संतप्य तत्पश्चात्पूर्ववत्सोपचारकैः ॥
1.68.m: Together, they amount to four hundred and forty-four. / Having offered libations thus, thereafter with the offerings of attendance as before,

1.68.s:
sarvābhīṣṭaṃ ca saṃprārthya praṇamyodvāsayetsudhīḥ /
bhādrakṛṣṇacaturthyādipratimāsamatandritaḥ //
1.68.d:
सर्वाभीष्टं च संप्रार्थ्य प्रणम्योद्वासयेत्सुधीः ।
भाद्रकृष्णचतुर्थ्यादिप्रतिमासमतन्द्रितः ॥
1.68.m: having prayed for all desires and bowed down, the wise one should bid farewell [to the deity]. / Beginning on the fourth day of the dark fortnight of Bhādrapada, each month, untiring,

1.68.s:
ārabhyārke dayaṃ mantrī yāvaccandrodayo bhavet /
tāvannopaviśedbhūmau jitavākkriyāmānasaḥ //
1.68.d:
आरभ्यार्के दयं मन्त्री यावच्चन्द्रोदयो भवेत् ।
तावन्नोपविशेद्भूमौ जितवाक्क्रियामानसः ॥
1.68.m: starting from sunrise until the rising of the moon, / the practitioner, controlling his speech, action, and mind, should not sit on the ground.

1.68.s:
tataścandrodaye mantrī pūjayedgaṇanāyakam /
pūrvoktavidhinā samyaṅnānāpuṣpopahārakaiḥ //
1.68.d:
ततश्चन्द्रोदये मन्त्री पूजयेद्गणनायकम् ।
पूर्वोक्तविधिना सम्यङ्नानापुष्पोपहारकैः ॥
1.68.m: Then, at moonrise, the practitioner should worship the Leader of the Gaṇas / according to the previously stated rule, properly, with various flowers and offerings.

1.68.s:
ekaviṃśatisaṃkhyākānmodakāṃśca nivedayet /
tadagre prajapenmantramaṣṭottarasahasrakam //
1.68.d:
एकविंशतिसंख्याकान्मोदकांश्च निवेदयेत् ।
तदग्रे प्रजपेन्मन्त्रमष्टोत्तरसहस्रकम् ॥
1.68.m: And he should offer twenty-one sweetmeats; / in front of him, he should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.

1.68.s:
tataḥ karpūrakāśmīraraktapuṣpaiḥ sacandanaiḥ /
ardhyaṃ dadyāttu mūlānte ṅeṃte gaṇapatiṃ tataḥ //
1.68.d:
ततः कर्पूरकाश्मीररक्तपुष्पैः सचन्दनैः ।
अर्ध्यं दद्यात्तु मूलान्ते ङेंते गणपतिं ततः ॥
1.68.m: Then, with camphor, saffron, and red flowers along with sandalwood, / he should offer water for the arghya with the root mantra followed by ‘gaṇapataye’ in the dative case.

1.68.s:
idamardhyaṃ kalpayāmi hṛdantor'dhyamanurmataḥ /
stutvā natvā visṛjyātha yajeccandramasaṃ punaḥ //
1.68.d:
इदमर्ध्यं कल्पयामि हृदन्तोर्ऽध्यमनुर्मतः ।
स्तुत्वा नत्वा विसृज्याथ यजेच्चन्द्रमसं पुनः ॥
1.68.m: ‘I prepare this water for the arghya’ ending with ‘namaḥ’ is regarded as the arghya mantra. / Having praised, bowed down, and dismissed [him], he should then worship the Moon again.

1.68.s:
ardhyaṃ dadyāñcaturvāraṃ pūjayitvā guruṃ tataḥ /
nivediteṣu viprāya dadyādardhāṃśca modakān //
1.68.d:
अर्ध्यं दद्याञ्चतुर्वारं पूजयित्वा गुरुं ततः ।
निवेदितेषु विप्राय दद्यादर्धांश्च मोदकान् ॥
1.68.m: He should offer the arghya four times, and then, having worshipped the guru, / he should give half of the offered sweetmeats to a brāhmaṇa.

1.68.s:
svayamarddhānprabhuñjīta brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ /
evaṃ vrataṃ yaḥ kurute samyaksaṃvatsarāvadhi //
1.68.d:
स्वयमर्द्धान्प्रभुञ्जीत ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः ।
एवं व्रतं यः कुरुते सम्यक्संवत्सरावधि ॥
1.68.m: He should himself eat the other half, practicing celibacy and mastering his senses. / The man who performs this observance properly for the duration of a year

1.68.s:
putrānpautrānsukhaṃ vittamārogyaṃ labhate naraḥ /
sūryodayādaśaktaścedastamārabhya mantravit //
1.68.d:
पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सुखं वित्तमारोग्यं लभते नरः ।
सूर्योदयादशक्तश्चेदस्तमारभ्य मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.68.m: obtains sons, grandsons, happiness, wealth, and good health. / If incapable of [fasting] from sunrise, the knower of mantras, beginning from sunset

1.68.s:
candrodayāntaṃ pūrvoktavidhinā vratamācaret /
evaṃ kṛte 'pi pūrvoktaṃ phalamāpnoti niścitam //
1.68.d:
चन्द्रोदयान्तं पूर्वोक्तविधिना व्रतमाचरेत् ।
एवं कृते ऽपि पूर्वोक्तं फलमाप्नोति निश्चितम् ॥
1.68.m: until moonrise, should perform the observance according to the previously stated rule. / Even when performed in this manner, he certainly obtains the aforementioned fruit.

1.68.s:
gaṇiśapratimāṃ dantidantena kapināpi vā /
gajabhagrena niṃbena sitārkeṃṇāthavā punaḥ //
1.68.d:
गणिशप्रतिमां दन्तिदन्तेन कपिनापि वा ।
गजभग्रेन निंबेन सितार्केंणाथवा पुनः ॥
1.68.m: Having fashioned an image of Gaṇeśa from an elephant's tusk or monkey-wood, / from a neem tree broken by an elephant, or from white arka wood,

1.68.s:
kṛtvā tasyāṃ samāvāhya prāṇasthāpanapūrvakam /
abhyarcya vidhivanmantrī rāhugraste niśākare //
1.68.d:
कृत्वा तस्यां समावाह्य प्राणस्थापनपूर्वकम् ।
अभ्यर्च्य विधिवन्मन्त्री राहुग्रस्ते निशाकरे ॥
1.68.m: and having invoked [him] in it after first infusing it with life-breath, / the mantra practitioner, worshipping [him] according to rule during a lunar eclipse,

1.68.s:
spṛṣṭrā caiva nirahārastāṃ śikhāyāṃ samudvahan /
dyūte vivāde samare vyavahāre jayaṃ labhet //
1.68.d:
स्पृष्ट्रा चैव निरहारस्तां शिखायां समुद्वहन् ।
द्यूते विवादे समरे व्यवहारे जयं लभेत् ॥
1.68.m: touching it and abstaining from food, bearing it upon his topknot, / shall attain victory in gambling, in dispute, in battle, and in legal affairs.

1.68.s:
bījaṃ varāho binddhāḍhyau manvindvānnau kalau tataḥ /
smṛtirmāṃseṃdumanvāgrā karṇocchiṣṭagaṇe vadet //
1.68.d:
बीजं वराहो बिन्द्धाढ्यौ मन्विन्द्वान्नौ कलौ ततः ।
स्मृतिर्मांसेंदुमन्वाग्रा कर्णोच्छिष्टगणे वदेत् ॥
1.68.m: The seed-syllable is the boar endowed with bindu; then the eleventh vowel endowed with moon and fire; / then memory endowed with flesh, moon, and fire; in [the mantra of] Ucchiṣṭa-Gaṇapati one should speak the ear;

1.68.s:
bakaḥ sadīrghapavano mahāyakṣāya yaṃ baliḥ /
balimantro 'yamākhyāto na cedvarṇo 'khileṣṭadaḥ //
1.68.d:
बकः सदीर्घपवनो महायक्षाय यं बलिः ।
बलिमन्त्रो ऽयमाख्यातो न चेद्वर्णो ऽखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.68.m: baka endowed with long wind, and ‘to the great yakṣa’ followed by ‘baliṃ namaḥ’— / this is declared to be the bali-mantra, granting all desires even if not [repeated] in syllables.

1.68.s:
praṇavo bhuvaneśānīsvabījānte navārṇakaḥ /
hastīti ca piśācīti likheñcaivāgriṃsuṃdarī //
1.68.d:
प्रणवो भुवनेशानीस्वबीजान्ते नवार्णकः ।
हस्तीति च पिशाचीति लिखेञ्चैवाग्रिंसुंदरी ॥
1.68.m: Beginning with the praṇava and the Bhuvaneśānī [seed] followed by its own seed-syllable, the nine-syllabled mantra consists of: / ‘hasti-piśāci-likhe svāhā’.

1.68.s:
navārṇo 'yaṃ samuddiṣṭo bhajatāṃ sarvasiddhidaḥ /
padaiḥ sarvaṇa mantreṇa pañcāṅgāni prakalpayet //
1.68.d:
नवार्णो ऽयं समुद्दिष्टो भजतां सर्वसिद्धिदः ।
पदैः सर्वण मन्त्रेण पञ्चाङ्गानि प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
1.68.m: This nine-syllabled [mantra] is declared to bestow all accomplishments on those who worship [him]. / One should assign the five limbs with the words of the entire mantra.

1.68.s:
anyatsarvaṃ samānaṃ syātpūrvamantreṇa nārada /
athābhidhāsye vidhivadvakratuṇḍamanuttamam //
1.68.d:
अन्यत्सर्वं समानं स्यात्पूर्वमन्त्रेण नारद ।
अथाभिधास्ये विधिवद्वक्रतुण्डमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.68.m: Everything else is identical to the previous mantra, O Nārada. / Now I shall explain according to rule the unsurpassed mantra of Vakratuṇḍa.

1.68.s:
toyaṃ vidhirvahniyuktakarṇendvāḍhyo haristathā /
sadīrgho dārako vāyurvarmānto 'yaṃ rasārṇakaḥ //
1.68.d:
तोयं विधिर्वह्नियुक्तकर्णेन्द्वाढ्यो हरिस्तथा ।
सदीर्घो दारको वायुर्वर्मान्तो ऽयं रसार्णकः ॥
1.68.m: Water, Vidhi accompanied by fire, and Hari endowed with ear and moon, / long dāraka, wind, ending in armor—this is the six-syllabled [mantra].

1.68.s:
bhārgavo 'sya muniśchando 'nuṣṭubdevo gaṇādhipaḥ /
vakratuṇḍābhidho bījaṃ vaṃ śaktiḥ kavacaṃ punaḥ //
1.68.d:
भार्गवो ऽस्य मुनिश्छन्दो ऽनुष्टुब्देवो गणाधिपः ।
वक्रतुण्डाभिधो बीजं वं शक्तिः कवचं पुनः ॥
1.68.m: Bhārgava is its seer; the metre is anuṣṭubh; the deity is the lord of Gaṇas / named Vakratuṇḍa; the seed-syllable is ‘vaṃ’; the energy is the armor.

1.68.s:
tāradṛnmadhyagairmantravarṇaiścandravibhūṣitaiḥ /
kṛtvā ṣaḍaṅgamantrārṇānbhrūmadhye ca gale hṛdi //
1.68.d:
तारदृन्मध्यगैर्मन्त्रवर्णैश्चन्द्रविभूषितैः ।
कृत्वा षडङ्गमन्त्रार्णान्भ्रूमध्ये च गले हृदि ॥
1.68.m: Making the six-limbed mantra syllables by means of the mantra syllables placed between tāra and dṛk and adorned with the moon, / [he should place them] between the eyebrows, at the throat, at the heart,

1.68.s:
nāmau liṅge pade nyasyākhilena vyāpakaṃ caret /
udyadarkadyutiṃ hastaiḥ pāśāṅkuśavarābhayān //
1.68.d:
नामौ लिङ्गे पदे न्यस्याखिलेन व्यापकं चरेत् ।
उद्यदर्कद्युतिं हस्तैः पाशाङ्कुशवराभयान् ॥
1.68.m: at the navel, at the genitals, and at the feet, and perform a pervasive placement with the whole [mantra]. / One should worship the elephant-faced one, possessing the radiance of the rising sun, bearing the noose,

1.68.s:
dadhataṃ gajavaktraṃ ca raktabhūṣāṃbaraṃ bhajet /
dhyātvaivaṃ prajapettarkalakṣaṃ dravyairdaśāṃśataḥ //
1.68.d:
दधतं गजवक्त्रं च रक्तभूषांबरं भजेत् ।
ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेत्तर्कलक्षं द्रव्यैर्दशांशतः ॥
1.68.m: goad, boon, and safety gestures in his hands, wearing red ornaments and garments. / Having meditated thus, he should recite [the mantra] six hundred thousand times, and perform fire oblations with one-tenth of that amount

1.68.s:
aṣṭabhirjuhuyātpīṭhe tīvrādisahiter'cayet /
mūrtiṃ mūrtena saṃkalpya tasyāmāvāhya pūjayet //
1.68.d:
अष्टभिर्जुहुयात्पीठे तीव्रादिसहितेर्ऽचयेत् ।
मूर्तिं मूर्तेन संकल्प्य तस्यामावाह्य पूजयेत् ॥
1.68.m: with the eight substances. He should worship on the ritual seat accompanied by Tīvrā and the others; / having envisioned the image through the embodied form, and having invoked [him] in it, he should worship [him].

1.68.s:
ṣaṭkoṇeṣu ṣaḍaṅgāni patreṣvaṣṭau tu śaktayaḥ /
yajedvidyāṃ vidhātrīṃ ca bhogadāṃ vipraghātinīm //
1.68.d:
षट्कोणेषु षडङ्गानि पत्रेष्वष्टौ तु शक्तयः ।
यजेद्विद्यां विधात्रीं च भोगदां विप्रघातिनीम् ॥
1.68.m: The six limbs are in the six angles, and the eight energies are upon the petals: / he should worship Vidyā, Vidhātrī, Bhogadā, Vipraghātinī,

1.68.s:
nidhipradīpāṃ pāpaghnīṃ puṇyāṃ paścācchaśiprabhām /
dalāgreṣu vakratuṇḍa ekadaṃṣṭramahodarau //
1.68.d:
निधिप्रदीपां पापघ्नीं पुण्यां पश्चाच्छशिप्रभाम् ।
दलाग्रेषु वक्रतुण्ड एकदंष्ट्रमहोदरौ ॥
1.68.m: Nidhipradīpā, Pāpaghnī, Puṇyā, and after that Śaśiprabhā. / On the tips of the petals are Vakratuṇḍa, Ekadaṃṣṭra, Mahodara,

1.68.s:
gajāsyalaṃbodarakau vikaṭau vidhnarāṭ tathā /
dhūmravarṇastato bāhye lokeśānhetisaṃyutān //
1.68.d:
गजास्यलंबोदरकौ विकटौ विध्नराट् तथा ।
धूम्रवर्णस्ततो बाह्ये लोकेशान्हेतिसंयुतान् ॥
1.68.m: Gajāsya, Lambodara, Vikaṭa, and also Vighnarāj, / and Dhūmravarṇa. Outside of that, [he should worship] the lords of the worlds accompanied by their weapons.

1.68.s:
evamāvaraṇairiṣṭvā pañcabhirgaṇanāyakam /
sādhaṃyedakhilānkāmānvakratuṇḍa praṃsādataḥ //
1.68.d:
एवमावरणैरिष्ट्वा पञ्चभिर्गणनायकम् ।
साधंयेदखिलान्कामान्वक्रतुण्ड प्रंसादतः ॥
1.68.m: Having thus worshipped the lord of Gaṇas through the five enclosures, / he shall accomplish all desires through the grace of Vakratuṇḍa.

1.68.s:
labdhvā gurumukhānmantraṃ dīkṣāsaṃskārapūrvakam /
brahmacārī haviṣyāśī satyavāk ca jitendriyaḥ //
1.68.d:
लब्ध्वा गुरुमुखान्मन्त्रं दीक्षासंस्कारपूर्वकम् ।
ब्रह्मचारी हविष्याशी सत्यवाक् च जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.68.m: Having received the mantra from the mouth of the guru after the initiation rite, / observing celibacy, eating sacrificial offerings, speaking truth, and with senses subdued,

1.68.s:
japedarkasahasraṃ tu ṣaṇmāsaṃ homasaṃyutam /
dāridṣaṃ tu parābhūya jāyate dhanadopamaḥ //
1.68.d:
जपेदर्कसहस्रं तु षण्मासं होमसंयुतम् ।
दारिद्षं तु पराभूय जायते धनदोपमः ॥
1.68.m: he should recite twelve thousand times for six months accompanied by fire oblations. / Overcoming poverty, he becomes equal to the giver of wealth [Kubera].

1.68.s:
caturthyādi caturthyantaṃ japedayutamādarāt /
aṣṭottaraśataṃ nityaṃ hutvā prāgvatphalaṃ labhet //
1.68.d:
चतुर्थ्यादि चतुर्थ्यन्तं जपेदयुतमादरात् ।
अष्टोत्तरशतं नित्यं हुत्वा प्राग्वत्फलं लभेत् ॥
1.68.m: From the fourth day [of the lunar fortnight] to the [next] fourth day, he should devoutly recite ten thousand times, / and having offered daily one hundred and eight fire oblations, he obtains the fruit as before.

1.68.s:
/
pakṣayorubhayormantrī caturthyāṃ juhuyācchatam /
apūpairvatsare sa syātsamṛddheḥ paramaṃ padam //
1.68.d:
।
पक्षयोरुभयोर्मन्त्री चतुर्थ्यां जुहुयाच्छतम् ।
अपूपैर्वत्सरे स स्यात्समृद्धेः परमं पदम् ॥
1.68.m: On the fourth day of both fortnights, the practitioner should offer a hundred fire oblations / with rice-cakes. In one year, he becomes the supreme abode of prosperity.

1.68.s:
aṅgārakacaturthyāṃ tu devamiṣṭvā vidhānataḥ /
haviṣā pā yasānnena naivedyaṃ parikalpayet //
1.68.d:
अङ्गारकचतुर्थ्यां तु देवमिष्ट्वा विधानतः ।
हविषा पा यसान्नेन नैवेद्यं परिकल्पयेत् ॥
1.68.m: On the fourth lunar day falling on a Tuesday, having worshipped the deity according to rule, / he should prepare an offering consisting of sacrificial food, milk-rice, and cooked grains.

1.68.s:
tato guruṃ samabhyarntya bhojayedvidhivatsudhīḥ /
niveditena juhuyātsaharasraṃ vidhivadvasau //
1.68.d:
ततो गुरुं समभ्यर्न्त्य भोजयेद्विधिवत्सुधीः ।
निवेदितेन जुहुयात्सहरस्रं विधिवद्वसौ ॥
1.68.m: Then the wise man, having worshipped the guru, should feed him according to rule; / with what has been offered, he should make a thousand fire oblations into the fire according to rule.

1.68.s:
evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ kṛtvā mahatīṃ śriyamāpnuyāt /
athānyatsādhanaṃ vakṣye lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
1.68.d:
एवं संवत्सरं कृत्वा महतीं श्रियमाप्नुयात् ।
अथान्यत्साधनं वक्ष्ये लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
1.68.m: Having done this for a year, he obtains great prosperity. / Now I will declare another procedure for the benefit of all people.

1.68.s:
iṣṭvā gaṇeśaṃ pṛthukaiḥ pāyasāpūpamodakaḥ /
nānāphalaistatomantrī haridrāmatha saindhavam //
1.68.d:
इष्ट्वा गणेशं पृथुकैः पायसापूपमोदकः ।
नानाफलैस्ततोमन्त्री हरिद्रामथ सैन्धवम् ॥
1.68.m: Having worshipped Gaṇeśa with flattened rice, milk-rice, cakes, and sweetmeats, / and various fruits, the practitioner should then take turmeric, rock salt,

1.68.s:
vacāṃ niṣkārddhabhāgaṃ ca tadarddhaṃ vā manuṃ japet /
viśodhya cūrṇaṃ prasṛtau gavāṃ mūtre vinikṣipet //
1.68.d:
वचां निष्कार्द्धभागं च तदर्द्धं वा मनुं जपेत् ।
विशोध्य चूर्णं प्रसृतौ गवां मूत्रे विनिक्षिपेत् ॥
1.68.m: and sweet flag in the amount of half a niṣka, or half of that, and recite the mantra over it. / Having purified the powder, he should drop a handful of it into cow's urine.

1.68.s:
sahasrakṛtvo manunā mantrayitvā prayatnataḥ /
snātāmṛtudine śuddhāṃ śuklāṃbaradharāṃ śubhām //
1.68.d:
सहस्रकृत्वो मनुना मन्त्रयित्वा प्रयत्नतः ।
स्नातामृतुदिने शुद्धां शुक्लांबरधरां शुभाम् ॥
1.68.m: Having carefully consecrated it a thousand times with the mantra, / the wise man, placing before the deity [a woman] who has bathed on her fertile day,

1.68.s:
devasya purataḥ sthāpya pāyayedauṣadhaṃ sudhīḥ /
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ vandhyāpi labhate sutam //
1.68.d:
देवस्य पुरतः स्थाप्य पाययेदौषधं सुधीः ।
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्नं वन्ध्यापि लभते सुतम् ॥
1.68.m: pure, wearing white garments, and auspicious, / should make her drink the medicine; even a barren woman obtains a son endowed with all auspicious marks.

1.68.s:
athānyatsaṃpravakṣyāmi rahasyaṃ paramādbhutam /
gocarmamātrāṃ dharaṇīmupalipya prayatnataḥ //
1.68.d:
अथान्यत्संप्रवक्ष्यामि रहस्यं परमाद्भुतम् ।
गोचर्ममात्रां धरणीमुपलिप्य प्रयत्नतः ॥
1.68.m: Now I shall proclaim another supreme and wonderful secret. / Having carefully smeared a piece of ground measuring a cow-hide,

1.68.s:
vikīrya dhānyaprakaraistatra saṃsthāpayeddhaṭam /
śuddhodakena saṃpūrya tasyopari nidhāpayet //
1.68.d:
विकीर्य धान्यप्रकरैस्तत्र संस्थापयेद्धटम् ।
शुद्धोदकेन संपूर्य तस्योपरि निधापयेत् ॥
1.68.m: and scattering various grains there, he should set up a water-pot. / Having filled it with pure water, he should place upon it

1.68.s:
kapilājyena saṃpūrṇaṃ śarāvaṃ nūtanaṃ śubham /
ṣaḍaṣṭākṣaramantrābhyāṃ dīpamāropayecchubham //
1.68.d:
कपिलाज्येन संपूर्णं शरावं नूतनं शुभम् ।
षडष्टाक्षरमन्त्राभ्यां दीपमारोपयेच्छुभम् ॥
1.68.m: an auspicious new earthen saucer filled with the ghee of a brown cow. / He should light an auspicious lamp with the six-syllabled and eight-syllabled mantras.

1.68.s:
dīpe devaṃ samāvāhya gandhapuṣpādibhiryajet /
snātāṃ kumārīmathavā kumāraṃ pūjayetsudhīḥ //
1.68.d:
दीपे देवं समावाह्य गन्धपुष्पादिभिर्यजेत् ।
स्नातां कुमारीमथवा कुमारं पूजयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.68.m: Having invoked the deity in the lamp, he should worship him with fragrant pastes, flowers, and the like. / The wise man should worship a maiden or a young boy who has bathed.

1.68.s:
dīpasya purataḥ sthāpyadhyātvā devaṃ japenmanum /
pradīpe sthāpite paśyeddvijarūpaṃ gaṇeśvaram //
1.68.d:
दीपस्य पुरतः स्थाप्यध्यात्वा देवं जपेन्मनुम् ।
प्रदीपे स्थापिते पश्येद्द्विजरूपं गणेश्वरम् ॥
1.68.m: Placing [the child] in front of the lamp and meditating on the deity, he should recite the mantra. / When the lamp is established, [the child] sees the lord of Gaṇas in the form of a twice-born.

1.68.s:
pṛṣṭastataḥ saṃpadi vā naṣṭaṃ caivāpyanāgatam /
sakalaṃ pravadedevaṃ kumārī vā kumārakaḥ //
1.68.d:
पृष्टस्ततः संपदि वा नष्टं चैवाप्यनागतम् ।
सकलं प्रवदेदेवं कुमारी वा कुमारकः ॥
1.68.m: Then, when questioned about prosperity, lost items, or the future, / the maiden or the young boy will recount everything.

1.68.s:
ṣaḍakṣaro hṛdantaścedbhavedaṣṭākṣaro manuḥ /
anye 'pi mantrā devarṣe santi tantre gaṇeśituḥ //
1.68.d:
षडक्षरो हृदन्तश्चेद्भवेदष्टाक्षरो मनुः ।
अन्ये ऽपि मन्त्रा देवर्षे सन्ति तन्त्रे गणेशितुः ॥
1.68.m: The six-syllabled mantra, if ending with ‘namaḥ’, becomes an eight-syllabled mantra. / There are other mantras too of the lord of Gaṇas in the Tantra, O divine sage.

1.68.s:
kintvatra yanna sādhyaṃ syātrriṣu lokeṣu sādhakaiḥ /
aṣṭaviṃśarasārṇābhyāṃ tanna paśyedapi kvacit //
1.68.d:
किन्त्वत्र यन्न साध्यं स्यात्र्रिषु लोकेषु साधकैः ।
अष्टविंशरसार्णाभ्यां तन्न पश्येदपि क्वचित् ॥
1.68.m: However, whatever cannot be accomplished here in the three worlds by practitioners / through the twenty-eight and six-syllabled mantras, one would never see anywhere.

1.68.s:
etadgaṇeśamantrāṇāṃ vidhānaṃ te mayoditam /
śaṭhebhyaḥ paraśiṣyebhyo vañcakebhyo 'pi mā vada //
1.68.d:
एतद्गणेशमन्त्राणां विधानं ते मयोदितम् ।
शठेभ्यः परशिष्येभ्यो वञ्चकेभ्यो ऽपि मा वद ॥
1.68.m: This procedure of the mantras of Gaṇeśa has been declared to you by me. / Do not speak it to villains, to disciples of others, or to cheats.

1.68.s:
evaṃ yo bhajate devaṃ gaṇeśaṃsarvasiddhidam /
prāpyeha sakalānbhoganinte muktipadaṃ vrajet //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde gaṇeśamantravidhānanirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.68.d:
एवं यो भजते देवं गणेशंसर्वसिद्धिदम् ।
प्राप्येह सकलान्भोगनिन्ते मुक्तिपदं व्रजेत् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे गणेशमन्त्रविधाननिरूपणं नामाष्टषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
1.68.m:
Whoever worships god Gaṇeśa, the giver of all perfections, in this manner, / having attained all enjoyments in this world, shall attain the state of liberation at the end.

Thus ends the sixty-eighth chapter, titled ‘Description of the Rules for the Mantras of Gaṇeśa’, in the third quarter of the great narrative of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.69.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
atha vakṣye trayīmūrtervidhānaṃ tvabjinīpateḥ /
mantrāṇāṃ yatsamārādhya sarveṣṭaṃ prāmuyāhṛvi //
1.69.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अथ वक्ष्ये त्रयीमूर्तेर्विधानं त्वब्जिनीपतेः ।
मन्त्राणां यत्समाराध्य सर्वेष्टं प्रामुयाहृवि ॥
1.69.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Now I shall declare the ritual procedure for the Lord of lotuses, who is the embodiment of the three Vedas, / by worshipping whose mantras one attains all desired things in the world.

1.69.s:
tāro recikayā yukto medhānetrayutā ratiḥ /
sasargā bāmakarṇoḍhyo bhṛgurvaḍhyāsano marut //
1.69.d:
तारो रेचिकया युक्तो मेधानेत्रयुता रतिः ।
ससर्गा बामकर्णोढ्यो भृगुर्वढ्यासनो मरुत् ॥
1.69.m: The syllable Oṃ joined with [the vowel] ṛ, the letter ra with e and the bindu, / with a visarga, then the letter sa endowed with the left ear [u], then the wind-syllable ya seated on fire [ra], with the long vowel ā,

1.69.s:
śeṣoditya iti prokto vasvarṇo bhuktimuktidaḥ /
devabhāgo muniśchando gāyatrī devatā raviḥ //
1.69.d:
शेषोदित्य इति प्रोक्तो वस्वर्णो भुक्तिमुक्तिदः ।
देवभागो मुनिश्छन्दो गायत्री देवता रविः ॥
1.69.m: followed by 'ādityāya'—this eight-syllabled mantra is proclaimed to grant enjoyment and liberation. / The sage is Devabhāga, the meter is gāyatrī, and the deity is the Sun.

1.69.s:
māyā vījaṃ ramā śaktirdṛṣṭādṛṣṭe niyogakaḥ /
satyāya hṛdayaṃ paścādbrahmaṇe śira īritam //
1.69.d:
माया वीजं रमा शक्तिर्दृष्टादृष्टे नियोगकः ।
सत्याय हृदयं पश्चाद्ब्रह्मणे शिर ईरितम् ॥
1.69.m: Māyā is the seed, Ramā the power, and the application is for seen and unseen fruits. / Then 'satyāya' is declared as the heart, 'brahmaṇe' as the head,

1.69.s:
viṣṇave tu śikhāvarma rudrāya parikīrtitam /
netraṃ syādagraye paścātśarvāyāsramudāhṛtam //
1.69.d:
विष्णवे तु शिखावर्म रुद्राय परिकीर्तितम् ।
नेत्रं स्यादग्रये पश्चात्शर्वायास्रमुदाहृतम् ॥
1.69.m: 'viṣṇave' is the crown lock, 'rudrāya' is proclaimed as the armor, / 'agnaye' is the eye, and thereafter 'śarvāya' is declared as the weapon.

1.69.s:
netro jvālā mano huṃ phaṭsvāhāntā manavo gaṇāḥ /
punaḥ ṣaḍarṇairhrī lakṣmyāḥ kṛtvāntaḥ sthaiḥ ṣaḍaṅgakam //
1.69.d:
नेत्रो ज्वाला मनो हुं फट्स्वाहान्ता मनवो गणाः ।
पुनः षडर्णैर्ह्री लक्ष्म्याः कृत्वान्तः स्थैः षडङ्गकम् ॥
1.69.m: The groups of mantras end in namaḥ, svāhā, vaṣaṭ, huṃ, vauṣaṭ, and phaṭ. / Then, with the six syllables of Hrī Lakṣmī situated within them, one performs the six limbs.

1.69.s:
śiṣṭāraujaṭhare pṛṣṭe tayorṅeṃtākhyayā nyaset /
ādityaṃ ca raviṃ paścādbhānuṃ bhāskarameva ca //
1.69.d:
शिष्टारौजठरे पृष्टे तयोर्ङेंताख्यया न्यसेत् ।
आदित्यं च रविं पश्चाद्भानुं भास्करमेव च ॥
1.69.m: On the remaining corners, the belly, and the back, one should place them in the dative case. / Then Āditya, Ravi, Bhānu, and Bhāskara,

1.69.s:
sūryaṃ ca mūrdhni vadane hṛdi guhye ca pādayoḥ /
sadyādipañca hrasvādyān nyasenṅeṃ hṛdayoṃ'timān //
1.69.d:
सूर्यं च मूर्ध्नि वदने हृदि गुह्ये च पादयोः ।
सद्यादिपञ्च ह्रस्वाद्यान् न्यसेन्ङें हृदयोंऽतिमान् ॥
1.69.m: and Sūrya—on the crown of the head, face, heart, private parts, and feet; / one should place the five beginning with Sadyojāta, prefixed with the short vowels and ending in the dative case with namaḥ.

1.69.s:
hrīṃ ramāmadhyagāmaṣṭau varṇāṃstārādikānnyaset /
mūrddhāsyakaṇṭhahṛtkukṣinābhiliṅgagudeṣu ca //
1.69.d:
ह्रीं रमामध्यगामष्टौ वर्णांस्तारादिकान्न्यसेत् ।
मूर्द्धास्यकण्ठहृत्कुक्षिनाभिलिङ्गगुदेषु च ॥
1.69.m: One should place the eight syllables beginning with Oṃ, having Hrīṃ and Ramā in the middle, / on the crown of the head, face, throat, heart, belly, navel, genitals, and anus.

1.69.s:
sacandrasvarapūrvaṃ tu ṅetaṃ śītāṃśumaṇḍalam /
mūrddhādikaṇṭhaparyantaṃ nyaseñcāndrimanuspraran //
1.69.d:
सचन्द्रस्वरपूर्वं तु ङेतं शीतांशुमण्डलम् ।
मूर्द्धादिकण्ठपर्यन्तं न्यसेञ्चान्द्रिमनुस्प्ररन् ॥
1.69.m: Prefixed with the moon-vowel and ending in the dative case, one should place the moon-circle / from the crown of the head down to the throat, meditating on the mantra of the moon.

1.69.s:
sparśānseṃdūnsamuñcārya ṅeṃtaṃ bhāskaramaṇḍalam /
nyasetkaṇṭhādinābhyantaṃ dhyāyanpradyotanaṃ hṛdi //
1.69.d:
स्पर्शान्सेंदून्समुञ्चार्य ङेंतं भास्करमण्डलम् ।
न्यसेत्कण्ठादिनाभ्यन्तं ध्यायन्प्रद्योतनं हृदि ॥
1.69.m: Uttering the stop-consonants endowed with the moon, ending in the dative case, one should place the sun-circle / from the throat down to the navel, meditating on the Illuminator in the heart.

1.69.s:
yādīnsacandrānuñcārya ṅetaṃ ca vahnimaṇḍalam /
nābhyādipādaparyantaṃ nyasedvahnimanusmaran //
1.69.d:
यादीन्सचन्द्रानुञ्चार्य ङेतं च वह्निमण्डलम् ।
नाभ्यादिपादपर्यन्तं न्यसेद्वह्निमनुस्मरन् ॥
1.69.m: Uttering the semi-vowels beginning with ya endowed with the moon, ending in the dative case, / one should place the fire-circle from the navel down to the feet, remembering the fire mantra.

1.69.s:
prokto 'yaṃ maṇḍalanyāso mahātejovidhāyakaḥ /
ādiṭhāntārṇapūrvaṃ ṅeṃnamontaṃ somamaṇḍalam //
1.69.d:
प्रोक्तो ऽयं मण्डलन्यासो महातेजोविधायकः ।
आदिठान्तार्णपूर्वं ङेंनमोन्तं सोममण्डलम् ॥
1.69.m: This nyāsa of circles, which confers great splendor, has been declared. / Preceded by the syllables beginning with a and ending in ṭha, ending in the dative and namaḥ, the moon-circle

1.69.s:
mūrddhādihṛdayāntaṃ tu vinyasetsādhakottamaḥ /
ḍakārādikṣakārāntavarṇādyaṃ pahnimaṇḍalam //
1.69.d:
मूर्द्धादिहृदयान्तं तु विन्यसेत्साधकोत्तमः ।
डकारादिक्षकारान्तवर्णाद्यं पह्निमण्डलम् ॥
1.69.m: the excellent practitioner should place from the crown of the head down to the heart. / Beginning with the syllables from ḍa to kṣa, ending in the dative case, the fire-circle

1.69.s:
ṅeṃtaṃ hṛdādipādāntaṃ vinyasetsusamāhitaḥ /
agrīṣomātmako nyāsaḥ kathitaḥ sarvasiddhidaḥ //
1.69.d:
ङेंतं हृदादिपादान्तं विन्यसेत्सुसमाहितः ।
अग्रीषोमात्मको न्यासः कथितः सर्वसिद्धिदः ॥
1.69.m: he should place, fully concentrated, from the heart down to the feet. / This nyāsa consisting of fire and moon has been declared to confer all accomplishments.

1.69.s:
nyasetseṃdūnmātṛkārṇāñjayāntapuruṣātmane /
namonte vyāpakaṃ mantrī haṃsnayāso 'yamīritaḥ //
1.69.d:
न्यसेत्सेंदून्मातृकार्णाञ्जयान्तपुरुषात्मने ।
नमोन्ते व्यापकं मन्त्री हंस्नयासो ऽयमीरितः ॥
1.69.m: Ending in namaḥ, one should place the mātṛkā syllables endowed with the moon onto the self of Puruṣa ending in jayā; / this pervasion is declared by the mantra practitioner as the Haṃsa-nyāsa.

1.69.s:
aṣṭāvaṣṭau svarāñśeṣānpañcapañca mitānpunaḥ /
uktādityamukhānetānvinyaseñca navagrahān //
1.69.d:
अष्टावष्टौ स्वराञ्शेषान्पञ्चपञ्च मितान्पुनः ।
उक्तादित्यमुखानेतान्विन्यसेञ्च नवग्रहान् ॥
1.69.m: Eight vowels, eight, the remaining ones, and then five and five measured again; / one should place these nine planets headed by the aforesaid Āditya

1.69.s:
ādhāraliṅgayornābhau hṛdi kaṇṭhe mukhāntare /
bhrūmadhye ca tathā bhāle brahmaraṅghre nyasetkramāt //
1.69.d:
आधारलिङ्गयोर्नाभौ हृदि कण्ठे मुखान्तरे ।
भ्रूमध्ये च तथा भाले ब्रह्मरङ्घ्रे न्यसेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.69.m: on the basal center, genitals, navel, heart, throat, inside the mouth, / between the eyebrows, forehead, and Brahmarandhra, in due order.

1.69.s:
haṃsākhyamagnīṣomākhyaṃ maṇḍalatrayameva ca /
punarnyāsatrayaṃ kuryānmūlena vyāpakaṃ caret //
1.69.d:
हंसाख्यमग्नीषोमाख्यं मण्डलत्रयमेव च ।
पुनर्न्यासत्रयं कुर्यान्मूलेन व्यापकं चरेत् ॥
1.69.m: One should perform the three nyāsas named Haṃsa, Agniṣoma, / and the three circles, and perform a pervasive nyāsa with the root mantra.

1.69.s:
evaṃ nyāsavidhiṃ kṛtvā dhyāyetsūryaṃ hṛdabuje /
dānābhayābjayugalaṃ dhārayantaṃ karai ravim //
1.69.d:
एवं न्यासविधिं कृत्वा ध्यायेत्सूर्यं हृदबुजे ।
दानाभयाब्जयुगलं धारयन्तं करै रविम् ॥
1.69.m: Having thus performed the rite of nyāsa, one should meditate on the Sun in the heart lotus: / Ravi bearing the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and a pair of lotuses in his hands,

1.69.s:
kuṇḍalāṃ gadakeyūrahāriṇaṃ ca trayītanum /
dhyātvaivaṃ prajapenmantrī vasulakṣaṃ daśāṃśataḥ //
1.69.d:
कुण्डलां गदकेयूरहारिणं च त्रयीतनुम् ।
ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेन्मन्त्री वसुलक्षं दशांशतः ॥
1.69.m: wearing earrings, armlets, bracelets, and necklaces, the embodiment of the three Vedas. / Having meditated thus, the mantra practitioner should recite [the mantra] eight hundred thousand times, and one-tenth of that

1.69.s:
raktāṃbhojaistilairvāpi juhuyādvidhivadvasau /
prathamaṃ pīṭhayajane dharmādīnāṃ sthale yajet //
1.69.d:
रक्तांभोजैस्तिलैर्वापि जुहुयाद्विधिवद्वसौ ।
प्रथमं पीठयजने धर्मादीनां स्थले यजेत् ॥
1.69.m: he should offer as fire oblations into the fire with red lotuses or sesamum according to the rule. / First, in the worship of the seat, he should worship in the place of Dharma and the rest;

1.69.s:
prabhūtaṃ vimalaṃ śāraṃ samārādhyamanantaram /
paramādimukhaṃ madhye khabiṃbāntaṃ prapūjayet //
1.69.d:
प्रभूतं विमलं शारं समाराध्यमनन्तरम् ।
परमादिमुखं मध्ये खबिंबान्तं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.69.m: having worshipped Prabhūta, Vimala, and Śāra next, / he should worship the head of the supreme beginning in the middle, ending in the sky-orb.

1.69.s:
somāgnimaṇḍalaṃ pūjyaravimaṇḍalamarcayet /
dīptā sūkṣmā jayā bhadrā vibhūtirvimalā tathā //
1.69.d:
सोमाग्निमण्डलं पूज्यरविमण्डलमर्चयेत् ।
दीप्ता सूक्ष्मा जया भद्रा विभूतिर्विमला तथा ॥
1.69.m: Having worshipped the circle of moon and fire, he should worship the circle of the sun: / Dīptā, Sūkṣmā, Jayā, Bhadrā, Vibhūti, Vimalā,

1.69.s:
amoghā vidyutā sarvatomukhī pīṭhaśaktayaḥ /
hrasvatrayoktijāḥ klībahī nā vahnīndusaṃyutāḥ //
1.69.d:
अमोघा विद्युता सर्वतोमुखी पीठशक्तयः ।
ह्रस्वत्रयोक्तिजाः क्लीबही ना वह्नीन्दुसंयुताः ॥
1.69.m: Amoghā, Vidyutā, and Sarvatomukhī are the powers of the seat. / Arising from the pronunciation of the three short vowels, lacking neuter letters, joined with fire and moon,

1.69.s:
svarā bījāni śaktīnāṃ tadādyāḥ pūjayettuḥ tāḥ /
brahmaviṣṇuśivātmā te sṛṣṭiḥ śeṣānvitāpyasau //
1.69.d:
स्वरा बीजानि शक्तीनां तदाद्याः पूजयेत्तुः ताः ।
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवात्मा ते सृष्टिः शेषान्विताप्यसौ ॥
1.69.m: the vowels are the seed-syllables of the powers; he should worship them beginning with those. / Consisting of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, this creation is joined with the remaining letters;

1.69.s:
evaṃ cānte yoga pīṭhātmane hṛdayamīrayet /
tārādyo 'yaṃ pīṭhamantrastvanenāsanamādiśet //
1.69.d:
एवं चान्ते योग पीठात्मने हृदयमीरयेत् ।
ताराद्यो ऽयं पीठमन्त्रस्त्वनेनासनमादिशेत् ॥
1.69.m: and thus at the end he should utter the heart mantra to the embodiment of the yoga-pīṭha. / This is the seat mantra beginning with Oṃ; with this he should assign the seat.

1.69.s:
dhruvo viyadbinduyutaṃ khaṃ khakholkāya dṛnmanuḥ /
navārṇāya ca manave mūrtiṃ saṃkalpayetsudhīḥ //
1.69.d:
ध्रुवो वियद्बिन्दुयुतं खं खखोल्काय दृन्मनुः ।
नवार्णाय च मनवे मूर्तिं संकल्पयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.69.m: The steady syllable [Oṃ], sky [ha] endowed with the bindu, kha, followed by 'khakholkāya'—this is the nine-syllabled eye-mantra; / for this nine-syllabled mantra the wise person should conceive the divine form.

1.69.s:
sākṣiṇaṃ jagatāṃ tasyāmāvāhya vidhivadyajet /
tataḥ ṣaḍaṅgāmārādhya dvikṣvaṣṭāṅgaṃ prapūjayet //
1.69.d:
साक्षिणं जगतां तस्यामावाह्य विधिवद्यजेत् ।
ततः षडङ्गामाराध्य द्विक्ष्वष्टाङ्गं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.69.m: Having invoked the witness of the worlds into it, he should worship him according to rule. / Then, having worshipped the six limbs, he should worship the eight limbs in the directions.

1.69.s:
saṃpūjya madhye vādityaṃ raviṃ bhānuṃ ca bhāskaram /
sūryaṃ diśāsu sadyādipañca hrasvādikānimān //
1.69.d:
संपूज्य मध्ये वादित्यं रविं भानुं च भास्करम् ।
सूर्यं दिशासु सद्यादिपञ्च ह्रस्वादिकानिमान् ॥
1.69.m: Having worshipped Āditya in the center, and Ravi, Bhānu, Bhāskara, / and Sūrya in the cardinal directions, with these five beginning with Sadyojāta prefixed with the short vowels,

1.69.s:
svasvanāmādivarṇādyāḥ śaktayor'cyā vidikṣu ca /
uṣāṃ prajñāṃ prabhāṃ saṃdhyāṃ tato brahmādikānyajet //
1.69.d:
स्वस्वनामादिवर्णाद्याः शक्तयोर्ऽच्या विदिक्षु च ।
उषां प्रज्ञां प्रभां संध्यां ततो ब्रह्मादिकान्यजेत् ॥
1.69.m: the powers should be worshipped in the intermediate directions, beginning with the first letters of their respective names: / Uṣā, Prajñā, Prabhā, and Saṃdhyā; then he should worship Brahmā and the others.

1.69.s:
purato 'ruṇamabhyarcya somaṃ jñaṃ ca guruṃ bhṛgum /
dikṣvaryamādikāniṣṭvā bhūmijaṃ ca śanaiścaram //
1.69.d:
पुरतो ऽरुणमभ्यर्च्य सोमं ज्ञं च गुरुं भृगुम् ।
दिक्ष्वर्यमादिकानिष्ट्वा भूमिजं च शनैश्चरम् ॥
1.69.m: Having worshipped Aruṇa in front, Soma, Jña [Budha], Guru [Bṛhaspati], and Bhṛgu [Śukra], / and having worshipped Aryaman and others in the directions, as well as the Son of Earth [Maṅgala] and Saturn,

1.69.s:
rāhuṃ ketuṃ ca koṇeṣu pūrvavatparipūjayet /
indrādyānapi vajrādyānpūjayetpūrvavatsudhīḥ //
1.69.d:
राहुं केतुं च कोणेषु पूर्ववत्परिपूजयेत् ।
इन्द्राद्यानपि वज्राद्यान्पूजयेत्पूर्ववत्सुधीः ॥
1.69.m: the wise person should worship Rāhu and Ketu in the corners as before; / he should also worship Indra and the others, as well as the thunderbolt and other [weapons], as before.

1.69.s:
itthaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivadbhāskaraṃ bhaktavatsalam /
samāhito dineśāya dadyādardhyaṃ dine dine //
1.69.d:
इत्थं संपूज्य विधिवद्भास्करं भक्तवत्सलम् ।
समाहितो दिनेशाय दद्यादर्ध्यं दिने दिने ॥
1.69.m: Having thus worshipped Bhāskara, who is affectionate to devotees, according to rule, / being concentrated, he should offer arghya day after day to the Lord of the day.

1.69.s:
prāṇānāyamya sadbhūmau nyāsānkṛtvā puroditān /
vidhāya maṇḍalaṃ bhānoḥ pīṭhaṃ pūrvavadarcayet //
1.69.d:
प्राणानायम्य सद्भूमौ न्यासान्कृत्वा पुरोदितान् ।
विधाय मण्डलं भानोः पीठं पूर्ववदर्चयेत् ॥
1.69.m: Having restrained the breaths upon pure ground, having performed the nyāsas spoken of earlier, / and having drawn the sun's maṇḍala, he should worship the seat as before.

1.69.s:
dhyātvārkaṃ prayajeddvivyairmānasairupacārakaiḥ /
pātraṃ tāmramayaṃ prasthatoyagrāhi suśobhanam //
1.69.d:
ध्यात्वार्कं प्रयजेद्द्विव्यैर्मानसैरुपचारकैः ।
पात्रं ताम्रमयं प्रस्थतोयग्राहि सुशोभनम् ॥
1.69.m: Having meditated on the Sun, he should worship him with divine, mental offerings. / A very beautiful copper vessel holding a prastha of water,

1.69.s:
nidhāya maṇḍale raktacandanādivinirmite /
vilomamātṛkāmūlamuñcaranpūrayejjalaiḥ //
1.69.d:
निधाय मण्डले रक्तचन्दनादिविनिर्मिते ।
विलोममातृकामूलमुञ्चरन्पूरयेज्जलैः ॥
1.69.m: placed within the maṇḍala made with red sandalwood and other substances, / he should fill with water while reciting the mātṛkā in reverse order and the root mantra,

1.69.s:
sūryabiṃbavinirgacchatsudhāṃbudhivibhāvitaiḥ /
kuṅkumaṃ rojanāṃ rājīṃ candanaṃ raktacandanam //
1.69.d:
सूर्यबिंबविनिर्गच्छत्सुधांबुधिविभावितैः ।
कुङ्कुमं रोजनां राजीं चन्दनं रक्तचन्दनम् ॥
1.69.m: meditated upon as an ocean of nectar flowing out of the sun's orb. / Saffron, yellow orpiment, black mustard, sandalwood, red sandalwood,

1.69.s:
karavīraṃ japāśālikuśaśyāmākataṇḍulān /
tilaveṇuyavāṃścaiva nikṣipetsalile śubhe //
1.69.d:
करवीरं जपाशालिकुशश्यामाकतण्डुलान् ।
तिलवेणुयवांश्चैव निक्षिपेत्सलिले शुभे ॥
1.69.m: oleander, hibiscus, rice paddy, kuśa grass, and grains of wild śyāmāka rice, / as well as sesame seeds, bamboo seeds, and barley he should cast into the auspicious water.

1.69.s:
sāṃgaṃ sāvaraṇaṃ tatrāvāhyārkaṃ pūrvavadyajet /
gandhapuṣpadhūpadīpanaivedyādyai rvidhānataḥ //
1.69.d:
सांगं सावरणं तत्रावाह्यार्कं पूर्ववद्यजेत् ।
गन्धपुष्पधूपदीपनैवेद्याद्यै र्विधानतः ॥
1.69.m: Having invoked the Sun there along with his limbs and retinue, he should worship him as before / with scents, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and the like, according to the injunctions.

1.69.s:
prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ kṛtvā kuryādaṅgāni pūrvavat /
sudhābījaṃ candanena dakṣe karatale likhet //
1.69.d:
प्राणायामत्रयं कृत्वा कुर्यादङ्गानि पूर्ववत् ।
सुधाबीजं चन्दनेन दक्षे करतले लिखेत् ॥
1.69.m: Having performed three breath controls, he should form the limbs as before. / He should write the nectar-seed with sandalwood paste on his right palm.

1.69.s:
tenācchādyārdhyapātraṃ ca japenmanumananyadhīḥ /
aṣṭottaraśatāvṛttyā punaḥ saṃpūjya bhāskaram //
1.69.d:
तेनाच्छाद्यार्ध्यपात्रं च जपेन्मनुमनन्यधीः ।
अष्टोत्तरशतावृत्त्या पुनः संपूज्य भास्करम् ॥
1.69.m: Covering the arghya vessel with that, he should recite the mantra with undivided mind / for a cycle of one hundred and eight times, and worship Bhāskara once again.

1.69.s:
hastābhyāṃ pātramādāya jānubhyāmavanīṃ gataḥ /
āmūrdhni pātramuddhṛtyāṃbareṇa varaṇe raveḥ //
1.69.d:
हस्ताभ्यां पात्रमादाय जानुभ्यामवनीं गतः ।
आमूर्ध्नि पात्रमुद्धृत्यांबरेण वरणे रवेः ॥
1.69.m: Taking the vessel with both hands, having touched the ground with his knees, / and raising the vessel up to his head, casting his gaze upon the sun in the sky,

1.69.s:
dṛṣṭiṃ cādhāya manasā pūjayitvā raviṃ punaḥ /
sādhakena svakaikyena mūlamantraṃ dhiyā japan //
1.69.d:
दृष्टिं चाधाय मनसा पूजयित्वा रविं पुनः ।
साधकेन स्वकैक्येन मूलमन्त्रं धिया जपन् ॥
1.69.m: and worshipping Ravi once more mentally, / with the practitioner reciting the root mantra in his mind in identity with him,

1.69.s:
ardhyaṃ dadyādraviṃ dhyāyavraktacandanamaṇḍale /
dattvā puṣpāñjaliṃ bhūyo japedaṣṭottaraṃ śatam //
1.69.d:
अर्ध्यं दद्याद्रविं ध्यायव्रक्तचन्दनमण्डले ।
दत्त्वा पुष्पाञ्जलिं भूयो जपेदष्टोत्तरं शतम् ॥
1.69.m: meditating on Ravi, he should offer the arghya into the red sandalwood maṇḍala. / Having offered a handful of flowers, he should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times again.

1.69.s:
nityaṃ vā tadvine 'pyevamardhyaṃ dadyādvivasvate /
tena tuṣṭo dineśo 'smai dadyādvittaṃ yaśaḥ sukham //
1.69.d:
नित्यं वा तद्विने ऽप्येवमर्ध्यं दद्याद्विवस्वते ।
तेन तुष्टो दिनेशो ऽस्मै दद्याद्वित्तं यशः सुखम् ॥
1.69.m: He should offer the arghya to Vivasvat daily, or even on that specific day. / Pleased thereby, the Lord of the day grants him wealth, fame, happiness,

1.69.s:
putrānpautrānabhīṣṭaṃ ca yadyatsarvaṃ prayacchati /
ardhyadānamidaṃ proktamāyurārogyavarddhanam //
1.69.d:
पुत्रान्पौत्रानभीष्टं च यद्यत्सर्वं प्रयच्छति ।
अर्ध्यदानमिदं प्रोक्तमायुरारोग्यवर्द्धनम् ॥
1.69.m: sons, grandsons, and whatever is desired—he bestows all of it. / This offering of arghya is declared to increase life and health.

1.69.s:
dhanadhānyapaśukṣemakṣetramitrakalatradam /
tejovīryayaśaḥkīrtividyāvibhavabhogadam //
1.69.d:
धनधान्यपशुक्षेमक्षेत्रमित्रकलत्रदम् ।
तेजोवीर्ययशःकीर्तिविद्याविभवभोगदम् ॥
1.69.m: It grants wealth, grain, cattle, well-being, fields, friends, and a wife; / it grants splendor, vigor, fame, renown, knowledge, prosperity, and enjoyments.

1.69.s:
gāyatryārādhanāsaktaḥ saṃdhyāvandanatatparaḥ /
evaṃ manuṃ japanvipro duḥkhaṃ naivāpnuyātkvacit //
1.69.d:
गायत्र्याराधनासक्तः संध्यावन्दनतत्परः ।
एवं मनुं जपन्विप्रो दुःखं नैवाप्नुयात्क्वचित् ॥
1.69.m: Devoted to the worship of the gāyatrī, intent upon the twilight prayers, / a Brahmin reciting the mantra in this way shall never encounter sorrow.

1.69.s:
vikartanāya nirmālyamevaṃ saṃpūjya dāpayet /
viyadvahnimarutsādyāntārvīseṃdusamanvitam //
1.69.d:
विकर्तनाय निर्माल्यमेवं संपूज्य दापयेत् ।
वियद्वह्निमरुत्साद्यान्तार्वीसेंदुसमन्वितम् ॥
1.69.m: Having thus worshipped the Sun, he should offer the previous day's floral offerings. / Endowed with ether, fire, wind, s, ā, d, y, ā, earth, and the moon [i.e., the seed-syllables],

1.69.s:
mārtaṇḍabhairavākhyaṃ hi bījaṃ trailokyamohanam /
biṃbabījena puṭitaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam //
1.69.d:
मार्तण्डभैरवाख्यं हि बीजं त्रैलोक्यमोहनम् ।
बिंबबीजेन पुटितं सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
1.69.m: is the seed-syllable named Mārtaṇḍabhairava, which enchants the three worlds; / enclosed within the solar-disc seed-syllable, it bestows the fruit of all desires.

1.69.s:
pūrvavatsakalaṃ cānyadatra jñeyaṃ manīṣibhiḥ /
bhṛgurjalendumanvāḍhyaḥ somāya hṛdayāntimaḥ //
1.69.d:
पूर्ववत्सकलं चान्यदत्र ज्ञेयं मनीषिभिः ।
भृगुर्जलेन्दुमन्वाढ्यः सोमाय हृदयान्तिमः ॥
1.69.m: Everything else here is to be understood by the wise as described before. / The letter of Bhṛgu [s], endowed with the water-letter [v], the moon [anusvāra], and the Manu [au], followed by 'somāya hṛdayāya namaḥ' [i.e. 'svauṃ somāya namaḥ']—

1.69.s:
ṣaḍakṣaro mantrarājo munirasya bhṛgurmataḥ /
chandaḥ paṅktistu somo 'sya devatā parikīrtitā //
1.69.d:
षडक्षरो मन्त्रराजो मुनिरस्य भृगुर्मतः ।
छन्दः पङ्क्तिस्तु सोमो ऽस्य देवता परिकीर्तिता ॥
1.69.m: this is the six-syllabled king of mantras; its seer is considered to be Bhṛgu, / its metre is Paṅkti, and Soma is declared to be its deity.

1.69.s:
ādyaṃ bījaṃ namaḥ śaktirviniyogo 'khilāptaye /
ṣaḍdīrgheṇa svabījena ṣaḍaṅgāni samācaret //
1.69.d:
