आद्यं बीजं नमः शक्तिर्विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ।
षड्दीर्घेण स्वबीजेन षडङ्गानि समाचरेत् ॥
1.69.m: The first syllable is the seed, 'namaḥ' is the power, and the ritual application is for the attainment of everything. / With its own seed-syllable lengthened through the six long vowels, one should perform the six limbs.

1.69.s:
pūrṇedvāsyaṃ sphaṭikabhaṃ nīlālakalasanmukham /
vibhrāṇamiṣṭaṃ kumudaṃ dhyāyenmuktāsrajaṃ vidhum //
1.69.d:
पूर्णेद्वास्यं स्फटिकभं नीलालकलसन्मुखम् ।
विभ्राणमिष्टं कुमुदं ध्यायेन्मुक्तास्रजं विधुम् ॥
1.69.m: With a face like the full moon, radiant like crystal, his face adorned with dark curls, / holding his wish and a night-lotus, wearing a pearl garland—one should meditate on the Moon.

1.69.s:
ṛtulakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ pāyasena sasarpiṣā /
juhuyāttaddaśāṃśena pīṭhe somāntapūjite //
1.69.d:
ऋतुलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं पायसेन ससर्पिषा ।
जुहुयात्तद्दशांशेन पीठे सोमान्तपूजिते ॥
1.69.m: One should recite the mantra six hundred thousand times, and with milk-rice mixed with clarified butter / offer oblations of one-tenth of that number on a ritual seat worshipped up to Soma.

1.69.s:
mūrtimūlena saṃkalpya pūjayedvidhivadvidhum /
kesareṣvaṅgapūjā syātpatreṣvetāśca śaktayaḥ //
1.69.d:
मूर्तिमूलेन संकल्प्य पूजयेद्विधिवद्विधुम् ।
केसरेष्वङ्गपूजा स्यात्पत्रेष्वेताश्च शक्तयः ॥
1.69.m:
Having projected the form with the root [mantra], one should worship the moon according to the rules.
In the filaments there should be worship of the limbs, and on the petals, these powers:

1.69.s:
rohiṇī kṛttikā caiva revatī bharaṇī puraḥ /
rātrirārdrā tato jyetsnā kalā hārasamaprabhā //
1.69.d:
रोहिणी कृत्तिका चैव रेवती भरणी पुरः ।
रात्रिरार्द्रा ततो ज्येत्स्ना कला हारसमप्रभा ॥
1.69.m:
Rohiṇī, Kṛttikā, Revatī, and Bharaṇī in front;
then Rātri, Ārdrā, Jyotsnā, and Kalā, whose radiance equals a necklace;

1.69.s:
suśuklamālyavasanāmuktāhāravibhūṣitāḥ /
sarvāḥstanabharākrāntā racitāñjalayaḥ śubhāḥ //
1.69.d:
सुशुक्लमाल्यवसनामुक्ताहारविभूषिताः ।
सर्वाःस्तनभराक्रान्ता रचिताञ्जलयः शुभाः ॥
1.69.m:
Adorned with pure white garlands and garments and pearl necklaces,
all heavy with the weight of their breasts, their folded hands raised, auspicious,

1.69.s:
svapriyāsaktamanaso madavibhramamantharāḥ /
samabhyarcyāḥ sarojākṣyaḥ pūrṇendusadṛśānanāḥ //
1.69.d:
स्वप्रियासक्तमनसो मदविभ्रममन्थराः ।
समभ्यर्च्याः सरोजाक्ष्यः पूर्णेन्दुसदृशाननाः ॥
1.69.m:
Their minds attached to their beloved, languid with the charm of intoxication;
these lotus-eyed maidens, whose faces resemble the full moon, should be worshipped.

1.69.s:
dalāgreṣu samabhyarcyāstvaṣṭau sūryādikā grahāḥ /
ādityabhūsutabudhamandadevejyarāhavaḥ //
1.69.d:
दलाग्रेषु समभ्यर्च्यास्त्वष्टौ सूर्यादिका ग्रहाः ।
आदित्यभूसुतबुधमन्ददेवेज्यराहवः ॥
1.69.m:
On the tips of the petals, the eight planets beginning with the sun should be worshipped:
Āditya, the son of the earth (Mars), Budha (Mercury), Manda (Saturn), the preceptor of the gods (Jupiter), Rāhu,

1.69.s:
śukraketuyutā hyete pūjyāḥ patragragāgrahāḥ /
raktāruṇaśvetanīlapītadhūmrasitāsitāḥ //
1.69.d:
शुक्रकेतुयुता ह्येते पूज्याः पत्रग्रगाग्रहाः ।
रक्तारुणश्वेतनीलपीतधूम्रसितासिताः ॥
1.69.m:
Accompanied by Śukra (Venus) and Ketu; these planets standing at the tips of the petals should be worshipped,
[having the colors] red, crimson, white, blue, yellow, smoky, white, and black.

1.69.s:
vāmorunyastataddhastā dakṣiṇena dhṛtābhayāḥ /
sokapālāṃstadastrāṇi tadvāhye pūjayetsudhīḥ //
1.69.d:
वामोरुन्यस्ततद्धस्ता दक्षिणेन धृताभयाः ।
सोकपालांस्तदस्त्राणि तद्वाह्ये पूजयेत्सुधीः ॥
1.69.m:
Their [left] hands are placed on their left thighs, and with the right they grant fearlessness.
The wise one should worship outside of that the guardians of the worlds and their weapons.

1.69.s:
eva saṃsādhito mantraḥ prayacchediṣṭamātmanaḥ /
paurṇamāsyāṃ jitāhāro dadyādardhyaṃ vidhūdaye //
1.69.d:
एव संसाधितो मन्त्रः प्रयच्छेदिष्टमात्मनः ।
पौर्णमास्यां जिताहारो दद्यादर्ध्यं विधूदये ॥
1.69.m:
The mantra mastered in this manner yields one's desire.
On the full moon day, having conquered one's food, one should offer an arghya at moonrise.

1.69.s:
maṇḍalatritaryaṃ kuryātprākpratyagāyataṃ bhuvi /
paścime maṇḍale sthitvā pūjādravyaṃ ca madhyame //
1.69.d:
मण्डलत्रितर्यं कुर्यात्प्राक्प्रत्यगायतं भुवि ।
पश्चिमे मण्डले स्थित्वा पूजाद्रव्यं च मध्यमे ॥
1.69.m:
One should make a triad of maṇḍalas on the ground extending from east to west;
standing in the western maṇḍala, and placing the articles of worship in the middle one,

1.69.s:
saṃsthāpya somamanyasminmaṇḍale 'bjasamanvite /
samabhyarcyaṃ vidhānena pīṭhapūjanapūrvakam //
1.69.d:
संस्थाप्य सोममन्यस्मिन्मण्डले ऽब्जसमन्विते ।
समभ्यर्च्यं विधानेन पीठपूजनपूर्वकम् ॥
1.69.m:
And having established the moon in the other maṇḍala endowed with a lotus,
and worshipped him according to rule, preceded by worship of the seat,

1.69.s:
sthāpayedrājataṃ pātraṃ puratastatra mantravit /
surabhīpayasāpūryya taṃ spṛśanprajapenmanum //
1.69.d:
स्थापयेद्राजतं पात्रं पुरतस्तत्र मन्त्रवित् ।
सुरभीपयसापूर्य्य तं स्पृशन्प्रजपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.69.m:
The knower of mantras should place a silver vessel before him there.
Filling it with cow's milk and touching it, he should recite the mantra

1.69.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ paścādvidyā mantreṇa mantravit /
dadyānniśākarāyārdhyaṃ sarvābhīṣṭārthasiddhaye //
1.69.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं पश्चाद्विद्या मन्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् ।
दद्यान्निशाकरायार्ध्यं सर्वाभीष्टार्थसिद्धये ॥
1.69.m:
One hundred and eight times; then the knower of mantras, with the vidyā-mantra,
should offer an arghya to the moon for the attainment of all desired aims.

1.69.s:
kuryādanena vidhinā pratimāsamatandritaḥ /
vaṣāntareṇa savaṣṭaṃ prāpnoti bhuvimānavaḥ //
1.69.d:
कुर्यादनेन विधिना प्रतिमासमतन्द्रितः ।
वषान्तरेण सवष्टं प्राप्नोति भुविमानवः ॥
1.69.m:
Performing this ritual every month without sloth,
a man on earth attains everything he wishes within a year.

1.69.s:
vidye vidyāmālini syādanta candriṇi katavadet /
candramukhi dviṭhānto 'yaṃ vidyāmantra udāhṛtaḥ //
1.69.d:
विद्ये विद्यामालिनि स्यादन्त चन्द्रिणि कतवदेत् ।
चन्द्रमुखि द्विठान्तो ऽयं विद्यामन्त्र उदाहृतः ॥
1.69.m:
‘vidye vidyāmālini’ should be [spoken], then at the end ‘candriṇi’, then one should say
‘candramukhi’, ending with ‘dviṭhā’ (svāhā); this is declared as the vidyā-mantra.

1.69.s:
evaṃ kumudinīnāthamantraṃ yo japati dhruvam /
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ sutānpautrānsaubhāgyaṃ labhate 'cirāt //
1.69.d:
एवं कुमुदिनीनाथमन्त्रं यो जपति ध्रुवम् ।
धनं धान्यं सुतान्पौत्रान्सौभाग्यं लभते ऽचिरात् ॥
1.69.m:
Whoever thus constantly recites the mantra of the lord of water-lilies
quickly obtains wealth, grain, sons, grandsons, and good fortune.

1.69.s:
athāṅgārakamantraṃ tu vakṣye dhanasutapradam /
tāro dīrghenduyugvyoma tadevenduyutaḥ punaḥ //
1.69.d:
अथाङ्गारकमन्त्रं तु वक्ष्ये धनसुतप्रदम् ।
तारो दीर्घेन्दुयुग्व्योम तदेवेन्दुयुतः पुनः ॥
1.69.m:
Now I shall declare the mantra of Aṅgāraka (Mars), which grants wealth and sons.
Tāra (Om), the ether (ha) joined with a long moon (ūṃ), then again that [same letter] with the moon,

1.69.s:
ṣāntaḥ sargī ca caṇḍīśau kramārdiduvisargiṇai /
ṣaḍarṇo 'yaṃ mahāmantro maṅgalasyākhileṣṭadaḥ //
1.69.d:
षान्तः सर्गी च चण्डीशौ क्रमार्दिदुविसर्गिणै ।
षडर्णो ऽयं महामन्त्रो मङ्गलस्याखिलेष्टदः ॥
1.69.m:
Ending with ṣa, with visarga (saḥ), and caṇḍīśa (bha) and u, each with a visarga (bhuḥ)—
this six-syllabled great mantra of Maṅgala grants all desired objects.

1.69.s:
virūpākṣo muniśchandogāyatraṃ devatā kujaḥ /
mantrārṇaiḥ ṣaḍbhiraṅgāni krurvandhyāyeddharātmajam //
1.69.d:
विरूपाक्षो मुनिश्छन्दोगायत्रं देवता कुजः ।
मन्त्रार्णैः षड्भिरङ्गानि क्रुर्वन्ध्यायेद्धरात्मजम् ॥
1.69.m:
Virūpākṣa is the sage, the metre is gāyatrī, Kuja is the deity.
Performing the limbs with the six syllables of the mantra, one should meditate on the son of the earth:

1.69.s:
meṣasthaṃ raktavasrāṅgaṃ śūlaśaktigadāvarān /
karairbibhrāṇamīśānasvedajaṃ bhūṃsutaṃ smaret //
1.69.d:
मेषस्थं रक्तवस्राङ्गं शूलशक्तिगदावरान् ।
करैर्बिभ्राणमीशानस्वेदजं भूंसुतं स्मरेत् ॥
1.69.m:
One should remember the son of the earth seated on a ram, his body and garments red,
bearing a spear, a lance, a mace, and granting boons with his hands, born from the sweat of the Lord.

1.69.s:
rasalakṣaṃ japenmantraṃ daśāṃśaṃ khadirodbhavaiḥ /
samidbhirjuhuyādagnau śaive pīṭhe yajetkujam //
1.69.d:
रसलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं दशांशं खदिरोद्भवैः ।
समिद्भिर्जुहुयादग्नौ शैवे पीठे यजेत्कुजम् ॥
1.69.m:
One should recite the mantra six hundred thousand times, and in the fire one should offer a tenth of that
with kindling sticks from the khadira tree; one should worship Kuja on a Śaiva seat.

1.69.s:
prāgaṅgāni samārādhya hyekaviṃśatikoṣṭakam /
maṅgalobhūmiputraśca ṛṇahartā dhanapradaḥ //
1.69.d:
प्रागङ्गानि समाराध्य ह्येकविंशतिकोष्टकम् ।
मङ्गलोभूमिपुत्रश्च ऋणहर्ता धनप्रदः ॥
1.69.m:
Having first worshipped the limbs, [one should worship] the twenty-one compartments:
Maṅgala, Bhūmiputra, the remover of debt, the giver of wealth,

1.69.s:
sthirāsano mahākāyaḥ sarvakarmāvarodhakaḥ /
lohito lohitākṣaśca sāmagānāṃ kṛpākaraḥ //
1.69.d:
स्थिरासनो महाकायः सर्वकर्मावरोधकः ।
लोहितो लोहिताक्षश्च सामगानां कृपाकरः ॥
1.69.m:
Sthirāsana, Mahākāya, Sarvakarmāvarodhaka,
Lohita, Lohitākṣa, Merciful to singers of the Sāman,

1.69.s:
dharātmajaḥ kujo bhaumo bhūmido bhūminandanaḥ /
aṅgārako mahīsūnuḥ sarvarogāpahārakaḥ //
1.69.d:
धरात्मजः कुजो भौमो भूमिदो भूमिनन्दनः ।
अङ्गारको महीसूनुः सर्वरोगापहारकः ॥
1.69.m:
Dharātmaja, Kuja, Bhauma, Bhūmida, Bhūminandana,
Aṅgāraka, Mahīsūnu, Remover of all diseases,

1.69.s:
vṛṣṭikartā vṛṣṭihartā sarvakāryārthasiddhidaḥ /
ityeka rviśatiḥ proktā mūrtayo bhūsutasya vai //
1.69.d:
वृष्टिकर्ता वृष्टिहर्ता सर्वकार्यार्थसिद्धिदः ।
इत्येक र्विशतिः प्रोक्ता मूर्तयो भूसुतस्य वै ॥
1.69.m:
Maker of rain, Withholder of rain, and Bestower of success in all undertakings;
these indeed are spoken of as the twenty-one forms of the son of the earth.

1.69.s:
maṅgalādīnyajenmantrī svasvasthānasthitānkramāt /
indrādyānapi vajrādīnevaṃ siddho bhavenmanuḥ //
1.69.d:
मङ्गलादीन्यजेन्मन्त्री स्वस्वस्थानस्थितान्क्रमात् ।
इन्द्राद्यानपि वज्रादीनेवं सिद्धो भवेन्मनुः ॥
1.69.m:
The practitioner of mantras should worship Maṅgala and the rest situated in their respective places in order,
and also Indra and the others, and the thunderbolt and the others; thus the mantra becomes perfected.

1.69.s:
sutakāmā kuraṅgākṣī bhaumavratamupācaret /
mārgaśīrṣe 'tha vaiśākhe vratāraṃbhaḥ praśasyate //
1.69.d:
सुतकामा कुरङ्गाक्षी भौमव्रतमुपाचरेत् ।
मार्गशीर्षे ऽथ वैशाखे व्रतारंभः प्रशस्यते ॥
1.69.m:
A fawn-eyed woman desirous of a son should perform the vow of Bhauma.
The commencement of the vow is praised in Mārgaśīrṣa or in Vaiśākha.

1.69.s:
aruṇodayavelāyāmutthāyāvaśyakaṃ punaḥ /
vinirvartya radāndhāvedapāmārgeṇa vāgyatā //
1.69.d:
अरुणोदयवेलायामुत्थायावश्यकं पुनः ।
विनिर्वर्त्य रदान्धावेदपामार्गेण वाग्यता ॥
1.69.m:
Rising at the time of dawn, and having performed
her necessary duties, she should clean her teeth with apāmārga, restraining her speech.

1.69.s:
snātvā raktāṃbaradharā raktamālyavilepanā /
naivedyādīṃśca saṃbhārānraktānsarvānprakalpayet //
1.69.d:
स्नात्वा रक्तांबरधरा रक्तमाल्यविलेपना ।
नैवेद्यादींश्च संभारान्रक्तान्सर्वान्प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
1.69.m:
Having bathed, wearing red garments, adorned with red garlands and unguents,
she should prepare all the provisions, including the food offerings, in red.

1.69.s:
yogyaṃ vipraṃ samāhūya kujamarcettadājñayā /
raktagogomayāliptabhūmau raktāsane viśet //
1.69.d:
योग्यं विप्रं समाहूय कुजमर्चेत्तदाज्ञया ।
रक्तगोगोमयालिप्तभूमौ रक्तासने विशेत् ॥
1.69.m:
Summoning a worthy brahmin, she should worship Kuja at his direction.
She should sit on a red seat upon ground smeared with red cow-dung.

1.69.s:
ācamya deśakālau ca smṛtvā kāmya samuccaran /
maṅgalādīni nāmāni svakīyāṅgeṣu vinyaset //
1.69.d:
आचम्य देशकालौ च स्मृत्वा काम्य समुच्चरन् ।
मङ्गलादीनि नामानि स्वकीयाङ्गेषु विन्यसेत् ॥
1.69.m:
Having sipped water, recalled the place and time, and stated her desire,
she should project the names beginning with Maṅgala onto her own limbs:

1.69.s:
mukhe pravinyasetsādhvī sāmagānāṃ kṛpākaram /
dharātmajaṃ nasorakṣṇoḥ kujaṃ bhaumaṃ lalāṭake //
1.69.d:
मुखे प्रविन्यसेत्साध्वी सामगानां कृपाकरम् ।
धरात्मजं नसोरक्ष्णोः कुजं भौमं ललाटके ॥
1.69.m:
The virtuous woman should place ‘Merciful to singers of the Sāman’ on the mouth,
‘Dharātmaja’ on the nose, ‘Kuja’ on the eyes, ‘Bhauma’ on the forehead,

1.69.s:
bhūmidaṃ tu bhruvormadhye mastake bhūminandanam /
aṅgārakaṃ śikhāyāṃ ca sarvāṅge ca mahīsutam //
1.69.d:
भूमिदं तु भ्रुवोर्मध्ये मस्तके भूमिनन्दनम् ।
अङ्गारकं शिखायां च सर्वाङ्गे च महीसुतम् ॥
1.69.m:
‘Bhūmida’ between the eyebrows, ‘Bhūminandana’ on the head,
‘Aṅgāraka’ on the tuft of hair, and ‘Mahīsūta’ on the whole body;

1.69.s:
bāhudvaye nyasetpaścātsarvarogāpahārakam /
mūrddhādi vṛṣṭikartāramāpādāntaṃ nyasetsudhīḥ //
1.69.d:
बाहुद्वये न्यसेत्पश्चात्सर्वरोगापहारकम् ।
मूर्द्धादि वृष्टिकर्तारमापादान्तं न्यसेत्सुधीः ॥
1.69.m:
Next, the wise woman should place ‘Remover of all diseases’ on both arms,
‘Maker of rain’ from the head down to the feet,

1.69.s:
vinyasedrṛṣṭihartāraṃ mūrddhāntaṃ caraṇāditaḥ /
nyasedante tato dikṣu sarvakāryārthasiddhidam //
1.69.d:
विन्यसेद्रृष्टिहर्तारं मूर्द्धान्तं चरणादितः ।
न्यसेदन्ते ततो दिक्षु सर्वकार्यार्थसिद्धिदम् ॥
1.69.m:
‘Withholder of rain’ from the feet up to the head;
then at the end she should place ‘Bestower of success in all undertakings’ in the directions.

1.69.s:
nābhau hṛdi śirasyāraṃ vakre bhūmijameva ca /
vinyasyaivaṃ nije dehe dhyāyetprāgvaddharātmajam //
1.69.d:
नाभौ हृदि शिरस्यारं वक्रे भूमिजमेव च ।
विन्यस्यैवं निजे देहे ध्यायेत्प्राग्वद्धरात्मजम् ॥
1.69.m:
Placing Āra on the navel, heart, and head, and Bhūmija on the mouth,
having thus performed the placement on her own body, she should meditate on the son of the earth as before.

1.69.s:
mānasairupacāraiśca saṃpūjyārdhyaṃ nidhāpayet /
ekaviṃśatikoṣṭhāḍhye trikoṇe tāmrapatrage //
1.69.d:
मानसैरुपचारैश्च संपूज्यार्ध्यं निधापयेत् ।
एकविंशतिकोष्ठाढ्ये त्रिकोणे ताम्रपत्रगे ॥
1.69.m:
Having worshipped him with mental offerings, she should present the arghya.
In a copper vessel containing a triangle rich with twenty-one compartments,

1.69.s:
āvāhyāṅgārakaṃ tatra raktapuṣpādibhiryajet /
aṅgāni pūrvamārādhya maṅgalādīnprapūjayet //
1.69.d:
आवाह्याङ्गारकं तत्र रक्तपुष्पादिभिर्यजेत् ।
अङ्गानि पूर्वमाराध्य मङ्गलादीन्प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.69.m:
Having invoked Aṅgāraka there, she should worship him with red flowers and other offerings.
Having first worshipped the limbs, she should worship Maṅgala and the rest.

1.69.s:
ekaviṃśatikoṣṭheṣu cakramāraṃ ca bhūmijam /
trikoṇeṣu ca sampūjya bahiraṣṭau ca mātṛkāḥ //
1.69.d:
एकविंशतिकोष्ठेषु चक्रमारं च भूमिजम् ।
त्रिकोणेषु च सम्पूज्य बहिरष्टौ च मातृकाः ॥
1.69.m:
Having worshipped Āra, the son of the earth, in the twenty-one compartments
and in the triangles, and the eight mothers outside,

1.69.s:
indrādīnatha vajrādīnbāhye saṃpūjayetpunaḥ /
dhūpadīpau samarpyātha godhūmānnaṃ nivedayet //
1.69.d:
इन्द्रादीनथ वज्रादीन्बाह्ये संपूजयेत्पुनः ।
धूपदीपौ समर्प्याथ गोधूमान्नं निवेदयेत् ॥
1.69.m:
She should again worship Indra and the others, and the thunderbolt and the others outside.
Then offering incense and a lamp, she should offer wheat food.

1.69.s:
tāmrapātre śuddhatoyapūrite raktacandanam /
raktapuṣpākṣataphalānyākṣipyārdhyaṃ samarpayet /
maṅgalāya tato mantrī idaṃ mantradvayaṃ paṭhet //
1.69.d:
ताम्रपात्रे शुद्धतोयपूरिते रक्तचन्दनम् ।
रक्तपुष्पाक्षतफलान्याक्षिप्यार्ध्यं समर्पयेत् ।
मङ्गलाय ततो मन्त्री इदं मन्त्रद्वयं पठेत् ॥

1.69.s:
bhūmiputra mahātejaḥ svedodbhavapinākinaḥ /
sutārthinī prapannā tvāṃ gṛhāṇārdhyaṃ namo 'stu te //
1.69.d:
भूमिपुत्र महातेजः स्वेदोद्भवपिनाकिनः ।
सुतार्थिनी प्रपन्ना त्वां गृहाणार्ध्यं नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.69.m:
‘O son of the earth, of great splendor, born from the sweat of the Wielder of the Pināka!
Desiring a son, I have taken refuge in you; accept this arghya, homage to you!

1.69.s:
raktapravālasaṃkāśa japākusumasannibha /
mahīsuta mahābhāga gṛhāṇārdhyaṃ namo 'stu te //
1.69.d:
रक्तप्रवालसंकाश जपाकुसुमसन्निभ ।
महीसुत महाभाग गृहाणार्ध्यं नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.69.m:
O one resembling red coral, like the hibiscus flower,
O son of the earth, highly fortunate one, accept this arghya, homage to you!’

1.69.s:
ekaviṃśatipūrvoktairṅenamontaiṃśca nāmabhiḥ /
tārādyaiḥ praṇametpaścāttāvatyaśca pradakṣiṇāḥ //
1.69.d:
एकविंशतिपूर्वोक्तैर्ङेनमोन्तैंश्च नामभिः ।
ताराद्यैः प्रणमेत्पश्चात्तावत्यश्च प्रदक्षिणाः ॥
1.69.m:
With the twenty-one previously mentioned names ending in the dative case and ‘namaḥ’,
beginning with Tāra (Om), she should then bow down, and perform that many circumambulations.

1.69.s:
dharaṇīgarbhasaṃbhūtaṃ vidyuttejaḥ samaprabham /
kumāraṃ śaktihastaṃ ca maṅgalaṃ praṇamāmyaham //
1.69.d:
धरणीगर्भसंभूतं विद्युत्तेजः समप्रभम् ।
कुमारं शक्तिहस्तं च मङ्गलं प्रणमाम्यहम् ॥
1.69.m:
‘I bow to Maṅgala, born from the womb of the earth, equal in brilliance to the flash of lightning,
a youth holding a lance in his hand.’

1.69.s:
tato rekhātrayaṃ kuryātkhadirāṅgārakeṇa ca /
mārjayedvāmapādena mantrābhyāṃ ca samāhitā //
1.69.d:
ततो रेखात्रयं कुर्यात्खदिराङ्गारकेण च ।
मार्जयेद्वामपादेन मन्त्राभ्यां च समाहिता ॥
1.69.m:
Then, with a charcoal of khadira wood, she should draw three lines,
and wipe them away with her left foot, composed in mind, with two mantras:

1.69.s:
duḥkhadaurbhāgyanāśāya putrasaṃtānahetave /
kṛtarekhātrayaṃ vāmapādenaitatpramārjmyaham //
1.69.d:
दुःखदौर्भाग्यनाशाय पुत्रसंतानहेतवे ।
कृतरेखात्रयं वामपादेनैतत्प्रमार्ज्म्यहम् ॥
1.69.m:
‘For the destruction of sorrow and misfortune, and for the sake of obtaining male offspring,
I wipe away these three drawn lines with my left foot.

1.69.s:
ṛṇaduḥ khavināśāya manobhīṣṭārthasiddhiye /
mārjayāmyasitā rekhāstisro janmatrayodbhavāḥ //
1.69.d:
ऋणदुः खविनाशाय मनोभीष्टार्थसिद्धिये ।
मार्जयाम्यसिता रेखास्तिस्रो जन्मत्रयोद्भवाः ॥
1.69.m:
For the destruction of debt and sorrow, and for the fulfillment of the desires of my heart,
I wipe away the three black lines arising from three births.’

1.69.s:
stuvīta dharaṇīputraṃ puṣpāñjalikarā tataḥ /
dhyāyantī tatpadāṃbhojaṃ pūjāsāṃgatvasiddhaye //
1.69.d:
स्तुवीत धरणीपुत्रं पुष्पाञ्जलिकरा ततः ।
ध्यायन्ती तत्पदांभोजं पूजासांगत्वसिद्धये ॥
1.69.m: Then, with folded hands holding a handful of flowers, she should praise the son of the Earth, / meditating on his lotus-feet for the successful completion of the worship:

1.69.s:
ṛṇahartre namastubhyaṃ duḥkhadāridrayanāśine /
saubhāgyasukhado nityaṃ bhava me dharaṇīsuta //
1.69.d:
ऋणहर्त्रे नमस्तुभ्यं दुःखदारिद्रयनाशिने ।
सौभाग्यसुखदो नित्यं भव मे धरणीसुत ॥
1.69.m: 'Homage to you, remover of debt, destroyer of sorrow and poverty! / O Son of the Earth, be ever the bestower of fortune and happiness upon me!

1.69.s:
taptakāñcanasaṃkāśa taruṇārkasamaprabha /
sukhasaubhāgyadhanada ṛṇadāridṣanāśaka //
1.69.d:
तप्तकाञ्चनसंकाश तरुणार्कसमप्रभ ।
सुखसौभाग्यधनद ऋणदारिद्षनाशक ॥
1.69.m: O one resembling molten gold, having the radiance of the morning sun! / O bestower of happiness, good fortune, and wealth, destroyer of debt and poverty!

1.69.s:
graharāja namaste 'stu sarvakalyāṇakāraka /
prasādaṃ kuru deveśa sarvakalyāṇabhājana //
1.69.d:
ग्रहराज नमस्ते ऽस्तु सर्वकल्याणकारक ।
प्रसादं कुरु देवेश सर्वकल्याणभाजन ॥
1.69.m: O king among planets, homage be to you, causer of all auspiciousness! / Grant your favor, O lord of deities, vessel of all auspiciousness!

1.69.s:
devadānavagandharvayakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ /
āpnuvanti śivaṃ sarve sadā pūrṇamanorathāḥ //
1.69.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः ।
आप्नुवन्ति शिवं सर्वे सदा पूर्णमनोरथाः ॥
1.69.m: Deities, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents / all attain auspiciousness, their desires always fulfilled.

1.69.s:
ācirādeva loke 'sminyasyārādhanato janāḥ /
prāpnuvanti sukhaṃ tasmai namo dharaṇisūnave //
1.69.d:
आचिरादेव लोके ऽस्मिन्यस्याराधनतो जनाः ।
प्राप्नुवन्ति सुखं तस्मै नमो धरणिसूनवे ॥
1.69.m: Homage to that son of the Earth, through whose worship people in this world / attain happiness without delay!

1.69.s:
yo vakragatimāpanno nṛṇāṃ duḥkhaṃ prayacchati /
pūjitaḥ sukhasaubhāgyaṃ tasmai kṣmāsūnave namaḥ //
1.69.d:
यो वक्रगतिमापन्नो नृणां दुःखं प्रयच्छति ।
पूजितः सुखसौभाग्यं तस्मै क्ष्मासूनवे नमः ॥
1.69.m: Homage to that son of the Earth who, entering retrograde motion, brings sorrow to mortals, / but when worshipped, brings happiness and good fortune!

1.69.s:
nabhasi dyotamānāya sarvakalyāṇahetave /
maṅgalāya namastubhyaṃ dhanasaṃtānahetave //
1.69.d:
नभसि द्योतमानाय सर्वकल्याणहेतवे ।
मङ्गलाय नमस्तुभ्यं धनसंतानहेतवे ॥
1.69.m: Homage to you, Maṅgala, shining in the sky, cause of all auspiciousness, / cause of wealth and offspring!

1.69.s:
prasādaṃ kuru me bhaumamaṅgalaprada maṅgala /
meṣavāhana rudrātmandehi putrāndhanaṃ yaśaḥ //
1.69.d:
प्रसादं कुरु मे भौममङ्गलप्रद मङ्गल ।
मेषवाहन रुद्रात्मन्देहि पुत्रान्धनं यशः ॥
1.69.m: Grant me your favor, O Bhauma, O Maṅgala, bestower of auspiciousness! / O one who rides a ram, whose nature is Rudra, grant me sons, wealth, and renown!'

1.69.s:
evaṃ stutvā praṇamyātha visṛjya dharaṇīsutam /
yathāśaktyā pradāya svaṃ gṛhṇīyādbraṇāśiṣaḥ //
1.69.d:
एवं स्तुत्वा प्रणम्याथ विसृज्य धरणीसुतम् ।
यथाशक्त्या प्रदाय स्वं गृह्णीयाद्ब्रणाशिषः ॥
1.69.m: Having thus praised him, bowed, and dismissed the son of the Earth, / one should give away one's wealth according to capacity and receive the blessings of Brahmins.

1.69.s: gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā bhuñjīyāttanniveditam //
1.69.d: गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा भुञ्जीयात्तन्निवेदितम् ॥
1.69.m: Having given the fee to the preceptor, one should eat what was offered to the deity.

1.69.s:
evamāvatsaraṃ kuryātpratimaṅgalavāsaram /
tilairhemaṃ vidhāyātha śatārddhaṃ bhojayoddvijān //
1.69.d:
एवमावत्सरं कुर्यात्प्रतिमङ्गलवासरम् ।
तिलैर्हेमं विधायाथ शतार्द्धं भोजयोद्द्विजान् ॥
1.69.m: One should do this for a year on every Tuesday. / Then, having made a fire oblation with sesame seeds, one should feed fifty Brahmins.

1.69.s:
bhaumamūrtiṃ svarṇamayīmācāryāya samarpayet /
maṇḍalasthe ghaṭe 'bhyarcyetsutasaubhāgyasiddhaye //
1.69.d:
भौममूर्तिं स्वर्णमयीमाचार्याय समर्पयेत् ।
मण्डलस्थे घटे ऽभ्यर्च्येत्सुतसौभाग्यसिद्धये ॥
1.69.m: One should present a golden idol of Bhauma to the preceptor; / one should worship him in a water-jar placed on a sacred diagram for the sake of attaining sons and good fortune.

1.69.s:
evaṃ vrataparā nārī prāpnuyātsubhagānsutān /
ṛṇanāśāya vittārthaṃ vrataṃ kuryātpumānapi //
1.69.d:
एवं व्रतपरा नारी प्राप्नुयात्सुभगान्सुतान् ।
ऋणनाशाय वित्तार्थं व्रतं कुर्यात्पुमानपि ॥
1.69.m: A woman devoted to this observance thus attains fortunate sons; / a man also should perform this observance for the eradication of debt and for wealth.

1.69.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ prajapenmantraṃmagnirmūrddheti vaidikam /
aṅgārakasya gāyatrīṃ vakṣye yajanasiddhaye //
1.69.d:
ब्राह्मणः प्रजपेन्मन्त्रंमग्निर्मूर्द्धेति वैदिकम् ।
अङ्गारकस्य गायत्रीं वक्ष्ये यजनसिद्धये ॥
1.69.m: A Brahmin should recite the Vedic mantra 'agnirmūrdhā…'. / I shall describe the gāyatrī of Aṅgāraka for the perfection of worship.

1.69.s:
aṅgārakāya śabdānte vidmahe padamīrayet /
śaktihastāya varṇānte dhīmahīti samuñcaret //
1.69.d:
अङ्गारकाय शब्दान्ते विद्महे पदमीरयेत् ।
शक्तिहस्ताय वर्णान्ते धीमहीति समुञ्चरेत् ॥
1.69.m: After the word 'aṅgārakāya', one should utter the word 'vidmahe'; / after the syllable ending in 'śaktihastāya', one should utter 'dhīmahi';

1.69.s:
tanno bhaumaḥ pracovarṇāndayānditi ca saṃvadet /
bhaumasyaiṣā tu gāyatrī japtuḥ sarveṣṭasiddhidā //
1.69.d:
तन्नो भौमः प्रचोवर्णान्दयान्दिति च संवदेत् ।
भौमस्यैषा तु गायत्री जप्तुः सर्वेष्टसिद्धिदा ॥
1.69.m: and one should recite the syllables 'tanno bhaumaḥ pracodayāt'. / This is the gāyatrī of Bhauma, which bestows the attainment of all desires upon the reciter.

1.69.s:
bhaumopāsanametaddhi budhamantramathocyate /
phaāntaḥ karṇendusaṃyukto budho ṅeṃte hadantimaḥ //
1.69.d:
भौमोपासनमेतद्धि बुधमन्त्रमथोच्यते ।
फआन्तः कर्णेन्दुसंयुक्तो बुधो ङेंते हदन्तिमः ॥
1.69.m: This is the worship of Bhauma; now the mantra of Budha is described: / The letter ending in ph [i.e., b], joined with the ear [u] and moon [anusvāra], 'budha' in the dative, followed by the heart-mantra ['namaḥ']—

1.69.s:
rasāṇoṃ budhamantro 'yaṃ munibrahmāsya kīrtitaḥ /
paṅktiśchaido devatā tu budhaḥ sarveṣṭado nṛṇām //
1.69.d:
रसाणों बुधमन्त्रो ऽयं मुनिब्रह्मास्य कीर्तितः ।
पङ्क्तिश्छैदो देवता तु बुधः सर्वेष्टदो नृणाम् ॥
1.69.m: this is the six-syllabled mantra of Budha; Brahmā is declared as its seer, / Paṅkti is the metre, and the deity is Budha, who grants all desires to mortals.

1.69.s:
ādyaṃ bījaṃ namaḥ śaktirviniyogo 'khilāptaye /
vande budhaṃ sadā bhaktyā pītāmbaravibhūṣaṇam //
1.69.d:
आद्यं बीजं नमः शक्तिर्विनियोगो ऽखिलाप्तये ।
वन्दे बुधं सदा भक्त्या पीताम्बरविभूषणम् ॥
1.69.m: The first syllable is the seed, 'namaḥ' is the power, and the ritual application is for the attainment of everything. / 'I revere Budha always with devotion, adorned with yellow garments,

1.69.s:
jānusthavāmahastāḍhyaṃ sābhayetarapāṇikam /
dhyātvevaṃ prajapesahasraṃ vijitendriyaḥ //
1.69.d:
जानुस्थवामहस्ताढ्यं साभयेतरपाणिकम् ।
ध्यात्वेवं प्रजपेसहस्रं विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.69.m: with his left hand placed upon his knee, and his other hand granting fearlessness'— / meditating thus, one with subdued senses should recite it a thousand times.

1.69.s:
daśāṃśaṃ juhuyādājyaiḥ pīṭhe pūrvoditer'cayet /
aṅgamātṛdiśāpālahetibhirbudhamarcayet //
1.69.d:
दशांशं जुहुयादाज्यैः पीठे पूर्वोदितेर्ऽचयेत् ।
अङ्गमातृदिशापालहेतिभिर्बुधमर्चयेत् ॥
1.69.m: One should offer one-tenth of that as oblations of clarified butter; one should worship him on the aforementioned ritual seat. / One should worship Budha along with his limbs, mothers, guardians of the directions, and weapons.

1.69.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī sādhayetsvamanorathān /
sahasraṃ prajapenmantraṃ nityaṃ daśadināvadhi //
1.69.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री साधयेत्स्वमनोरथान् ।
सहस्रं प्रजपेन्मन्त्रं नित्यं दशदिनावधि ॥
1.69.m: When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner achieves his desires. / If one recites the mantra a thousand times daily for a period of ten days,

1.69.s:
tasyāśu grahajā pīḍā naśyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ /
budhasyārādhanaṃ proktaṃ gurorārādhanaṃ śṛṇu //
1.69.d:
तस्याशु ग्रहजा पीडा नश्यत्येव न संशयः ।
बुधस्याराधनं प्रोक्तं गुरोराराधनं शृणु ॥
1.69.m: the affliction caused by the planet certainly vanishes for him, without a doubt. / The worship of Budha has been spoken; now hear the worship of Guru.

1.69.s:
bṛṃhaspatipadaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ seṃdvādyarṇāghamaṇḍitam /
namonto vasuvarṇo 'yaṃ munirbrahmāsya saṃmataḥ //
1.69.d:
बृंहस्पतिपदं ङेंतं सेंद्वाद्यर्णाघमण्डितम् ।
नमोन्तो वसुवर्णो ऽयं मुनिर्ब्रह्मास्य संमतः ॥
1.69.m: The word 'bṛhaspati' in the dative case, adorned with the first letter [a] with the moon [anusvāra], / ending with 'namaḥ' [i.e. 'oṃ bṛhaspataye namaḥ'], is an eight-syllabled mantra; Brahmā is accepted as its seer,

1.69.s:
chando 'nuṣṭupsurācāryo devatā bījamādimam /
hṛcchaktirdīrghavahnīnduyugalenāṅgakalpanā //
1.69.d:
छन्दो ऽनुष्टुप्सुराचार्यो देवता बीजमादिमम् ।
हृच्छक्तिर्दीर्घवह्नीन्दुयुगलेनाङ्गकल्पना ॥
1.69.m: the metre is Anuṣṭubh, the teacher of the gods is the deity, the first syllable is the seed, / 'namaḥ' is the power, and the assignment of limbs is made with the long vowels accompanied by fire and the moon.

1.69.s:
nyastavāmakaraṃ rāśau ratnānāṃ dakṣiṇātkarāt /
kirantaṃ pītapuṣpālaṅkārālepāṃśukārcitam //
1.69.d:
न्यस्तवामकरं राशौ रत्नानां दक्षिणात्करात् ।
किरन्तं पीतपुष्पालङ्कारालेपांशुकार्चितम् ॥
1.69.m: Resting his left hand upon a heap of gems, scattering [wealth] from his right hand, / worshipped with yellow flowers, ornaments, ointments, and garments,

1.69.s:
sarvavidyānidhiṃ devaguruṃ svarṇadyutiṃ smaret /
lakṣaṃ japo daśāṃśena ghṛtenānnena vā hunet //
1.69.d:
सर्वविद्यानिधिं देवगुरुं स्वर्णद्युतिं स्मरेत् ।
लक्षं जपो दशांशेन घृतेनान्नेन वा हुनेत् ॥
1.69.m: one should meditate on the teacher of the gods, the treasury of all knowledge, possessing a golden lustre. / The recitation is a hundred thousand times; one-tenth of that should be offered into the fire with clarified butter or food.

1.69.s:
dharmādipīṭhe prayajedaṅgadikpālahetibhiḥ /
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī sādhayediṣṭamātmanaḥ //
1.69.d:
धर्मादिपीठे प्रयजेदङ्गदिक्पालहेतिभिः ।
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री साधयेदिष्टमात्मनः ॥
1.69.m: One should worship on the seat of Dharma and the rest, with the limbs, guardians of the directions, and their weapons. / When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner achieves his desired object.

1.69.s:
viparogādipīḍāsu kalahe svajanodbhave /
pippalotthasamidbhiśca juhuyāttannivṛttaye //
1.69.d:
विपरोगादिपीडासु कलहे स्वजनोद्भवे ।
पिप्पलोत्थसमिद्भिश्च जुहुयात्तन्निवृत्तये ॥
1.69.m: In afflictions such as fever, sickness, and the like, or in strife arising among one's own kinsmen, / one should offer oblations with sacred fuel sticks of the pippala tree for their cessation.

1.69.s:
hutvā dinatrayaṃ mantrī niśāpuṣpairghṛtaplutaiḥ /
sa viṃśatiśataṃ śīghraṃ vāsāṃsi labhate mahīm //
1.69.d:
हुत्वा दिनत्रयं मन्त्री निशापुष्पैर्घृतप्लुतैः ।
स विंशतिशतं शीघ्रं वासांसि लभते महीम् ॥
1.69.m: Having offered oblations for three days with night-blooming flowers drenched in clarified butter, / the practitioner quickly obtains garments, land, and one hundred and twenty [cows].

1.69.s:
gurorārādhanaṃ proktaṃ śṛṇu śukrasya sāṃpratam /
vasraṃ me dehi śukrāya ṭhadvayānto dhruvādikaḥ //
1.69.d:
गुरोराराधनं प्रोक्तं शृणु शुक्रस्य सांप्रतम् ।
वस्रं मे देहि शुक्राय ठद्वयान्तो ध्रुवादिकः ॥
1.69.m: The worship of Guru has been spoken; now hear that of Śukra: / 'vastraṃ me dehi śukrāya' ending with two ṭhas ['svāhā'] and beginning with dhruva ['oṃ']—

1.69.s:
rudrārṇo 'yaṃ manurbrahmā muniśchando virāhuta /
daityejyo devatā bījaṃ dhruvaḥ śaktirvasupriyā //
1.69.d:
रुद्रार्णो ऽयं मनुर्ब्रह्मा मुनिश्छन्दो विराहुत ।
दैत्येज्यो देवता बीजं ध्रुवः शक्तिर्वसुप्रिया ॥
1.69.m: this eleven-syllabled mantra has Brahmā as its seer, the metre is Virāj, / the preceptor of the Daityas is the deity, dhruva ['oṃ'] is the seed, and the beloved of the Vasus ['svāhā'] is the power.

1.69.s:
bhūnetra candranetrāgninetrārṇaiḥ syātṣaḍaṅgakam /
śuklāṃbarālepabhūṣaṃ kareṇa dadataṃ dhanam //
1.69.d:
भूनेत्र चन्द्रनेत्राग्निनेत्रार्णैः स्यात्षडङ्गकम् ।
शुक्लांबरालेपभूषं करेण ददतं धनम् ॥
1.69.m: The six limbs are formed with the syllables with one, two, three, four, five, and six vowels. / Adorned with white garments, ointments, and ornaments, granting wealth with one hand,

1.69.s:
vāmena śukraṃ vyākhyānamudrādoṣaṃ smaretsudhīḥ /
ayutaṃ prajapenmantraṃ daśāṃśaṃ juhuyād ghṛtaiḥ //
1.69.d:
वामेन शुक्रं व्याख्यानमुद्रादोषं स्मरेत्सुधीः ।
अयुतं प्रजपेन्मन्त्रं दशांशं जुहुयाद् घृतैः ॥
1.69.m: and showing the gesture of exposition with the left, the wise man should meditate on Śukra. / One should recite the mantra ten thousand times and offer one-tenth of that as oblations with clarified butter.

1.69.s:
dharmādipīṭhe prayajedaṅgendrāditadāyudhaiḥ /
śvetapuṣpaiḥ sugandhaiśca juhuyād bhṛguvāsare //
1.69.d:
धर्मादिपीठे प्रयजेदङ्गेन्द्रादितदायुधैः ।
श्वेतपुष्पैः सुगन्धैश्च जुहुयाद् भृगुवासरे ॥
1.69.m: One should worship on the seat of Dharma and the rest, along with the limbs, Indra and the other [guardians], and their weapons. / On Friday, one should offer oblations with white, fragrant flowers.

1.69.s:
ekaviṃśativāraṃ yo labhatesoṃ'śukaṃ maṇīn /
manavo 'mo sadā gopyā na deyā yasya kasyacit //
1.69.d:
एकविंशतिवारं यो लभतेसोंऽशुकं मणीन् ।
मनवो ऽमो सदा गोप्या न देया यस्य कस्यचित् ॥
1.69.m: One who [recites] twenty-one times obtains garments and gems. / These mantras should always be kept secret, and not given to just anyone;

1.69.s:
bhaktiyuktāya śiṣyāya deyā vā nijasūnave //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde mantravidhānanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikonasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.69.d:
भक्तियुक्ताय शिष्याय देया वा निजसूनवे ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे मन्त्रविधाननिरूपणं नामैकोनसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः
1.69.m:
they may be given to a devoted disciple, or to one's own son.

Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Rules for Mantras', in the third quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the Pūrvabhāga of the illustrious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
